title.zh: 卷二百七十八 列傳第三十七 馬全義 雷德驤 王超
title.en: Volume 278 Biographies 37: Ma Quanyi, Lei Dexiang, Wang Chao
title.raw: 卷二百七十八 列傳第三十七 馬全義 雷德驤 王超 Volume 278 Biographies 37: Ma Quanyi, Lei Dexiang, Wang Chao

sentences.zh: 馬全義

translations.literal: Ma Quanyi
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quanyi

sentences.zh: 馬全義，幽州薊人。

translations.literal: Ma Quanyi was a man of Ji in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quanyi was from Ji in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 十餘歲學擊劍，善騎射。

translations.literal: From his teens he studied swordplay and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: From his teens he trained in swordplay and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 十五，隸魏帥范延光帳下。

translations.literal: At fifteen he entered the service of Fan Yanguang, military governor of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he entered the service of Fan Yanguang, military governor of Wei.

sentences.zh: 延光叛，晉祖征之，以城降，悉籍所部來上。

translations.literal: When Yanguang rebelled, the founder of Later Jin marched against him; he surrendered the city, and all his troops were registered and presented to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanguang rebelled, the Jin founder attacked him; Yanguang surrendered the city and registered his entire command for imperial service.

sentences.zh: 全義在籍中，因補禁軍。

translations.literal: Quanyi was on the roll and was accordingly appointed to the Palace Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi was on the roll and was appointed to the Palace Corps.

sentences.zh: 以不得志，遂遁去。

translations.literal: Frustrated in his ambitions, he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Unhappy with his prospects, he fled.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，李守貞鎮河中，召置帳下。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era of Later Han, Li Shouzhen governed Hezhong and summoned him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou era of Later Han, Li Shouzhen governed Hezhong and took Quanyi onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 及守貞叛，周祖討之，全義每率敢死士，夜出攻周祖壘，多所殺傷。

translations.literal: When Shouzhen rebelled, the founder of Later Zhou attacked him; Quanyi repeatedly led dare-to-die troops in night assaults on the Zhou camp, killing and wounding many.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouzhen rebelled, the Zhou founder attacked him; Quanyi repeatedly led dare-to-die troops in night raids on the Zhou camp, killing and wounding many.

sentences.zh: 守貞貪而無謀，性多忌克，全義屢為畫策，皆不能用。

translations.literal: Shouzhen was greedy and without strategy, jealous and harsh by nature; Quanyi often counseled him, but none of his plans was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen was greedy, unstrategic, and jealous; Quanyi often advised him, but none of his counsel was heeded.

sentences.zh: 城陷，遂變姓名亡命。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he changed his name and fled for his life.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he changed his name and fled.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，世宗鎮澶淵，全義往事之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun in Zhou, Shizong governed Chanyuan; Quanyi went to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Guangshun, Shizong governed Chanyuan and Quanyi went to serve him.

sentences.zh: 從世宗入朝，周祖召見，補殿前指揮使，謂左右曰：「此人忠於所事，昔在河中，屢挫吾軍，汝等宜效之。」

translations.literal: When he followed Shizong to court, Zhou Taizu summoned him, appointed him commander of the Front Palace Guard, and said to those beside him: "This man was loyal to his former master; at Hezhong he repeatedly defeated our army—you should take him as your model."
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Shizong to court, Taizu of Zhou summoned him, made him commander of the Front Palace Guard, and told his attendants, "This man was loyal to his master; at Hezhong he repeatedly beat our army—you should emulate him."

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遷右番行首。

translations.literal: When Shizong acceded, Quanyi was transferred to chief of the right rotating guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne, Quanyi was made chief of the right rotating guard.

sentences.zh: 從世宗戰高平，以功遷散員指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed Shizong in the battle of Gaoping and, for merit, was promoted commander of miscellaneous guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with Shizong at Gaoping and, for merit, was promoted commander of miscellaneous guard troops.

sentences.zh: 從征淮南，以功遷殿前指揮使、右番都虞候。

translations.literal: On the Huainan campaign he was promoted commander of the Front Palace Guard and chief adjutant of the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: On the Huainan campaign he rose to commander of the Front Palace Guard and chief adjutant of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，授鐵騎左第二軍都校，領播州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gongdi acceded, he was made commander of the second company, left wing, Iron Cavalry, and regimental commissioner of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongdi succeeded, he was made commander of the second left-wing Iron Cavalry company and regimental commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，歷內殿直都知、控鶴左廂都校，領果州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he served successively as director of the Inner Hall Direct Guard and commander of the left wing, Crane Control, and was made regimental commissioner of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he served as director of the Inner Hall Direct Guard and commander of the left wing of Crane Control, and was made regimental commissioner of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 從征李筠，筠退保澤州，城小而固，攻之未下，太祖患之，召全義賜食御榻前問計，對曰：「筠守孤城，若並力急攻，立可殄滅，儻緩之，適足長其奸爾。」

translations.literal: On the campaign against Li Jun, Jun withdrew to hold Ze Prefecture; the city was small but strong and could not be taken at once. Taizu was worried and summoned Quanyi, fed him at the imperial couch, and asked his plan. He replied: "Jun holds a lone city; if we concentrate our force and press the attack, he can be destroyed at once; if we delay, we only nurture his treachery."
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Li Jun, Jun withdrew to Ze Prefecture; the city was small but strong and would not fall quickly. Taizu was troubled, summoned Quanyi, and fed him before the imperial couch to ask his plan. Quanyi replied, "Jun holds a lone city; concentrate force and press the attack and he can be destroyed at once; delay only feeds his treachery."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「此吾心也。」

translations.literal: Taizu said: "That is exactly my thought."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "That is exactly what I think."

sentences.zh: 即麾兵急擊之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered the army to press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered a fierce assault.

sentences.zh: 全義率敢死士數十人乘城，攀堞而上，為飛矢貫臂，流血被體。

translations.literal: Quanyi led several dozen dare-to-die men up the wall, climbing the battlements; a flying arrow pierced his arm and blood soaked his body.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi led several dozen dare-to-die men up the wall; a flying arrow pierced his arm and blood soaked him.

sentences.zh: 全義拔鏃臨敵，士氣益奮，遂克其城。

translations.literal: Quanyi pulled out the arrow and faced the enemy; the troops' fighting spirit surged, and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled out the arrow and kept fighting; morale surged and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 遷虎捷左廂都校，領睦州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commander of the left wing, Tiger Swift Army, and made defense commissioner of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commander of the left wing of the Tiger Swift Army and made defense commissioner of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 又從征李重進，領控鶴、虎捷兩軍為後殿。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Li Chongjin he led the Crane Control and Tiger Swift armies as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Li Chongjin he commanded the Crane Control and Tiger Swift armies as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 賊平班師，錄功居多，改龍捷左廂都校，領江州防禦使，俄被疾。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified and the army returned, his achievements ranked among the greatest; he was made commander of the left wing, Dragon Swift Army, and defense commissioner of Jiang Prefecture; soon he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were crushed and the army returned, his merit ranked first; he was made commander of the left Dragon Swift wing and defense commissioner of Jiang Prefecture, but soon fell ill.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣太醫診視，仍諭密旨曰：「俟疾間，當授以河陽節制。」

translations.literal: Taizu sent the imperial physician to examine him and delivered a secret order: "When your illness eases, you shall be given the He-Yang military governorship."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent the imperial physician and a secret message: "When you recover, you shall receive the He-Yang military governorship."

sentences.zh: 全義疾已亟，但叩頭謝。

translations.literal: Quanyi's illness was already grave; he could only bow his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi was already gravely ill and could only bow in thanks.

sentences.zh: 數日卒，年三十八。

translations.literal: Within days he died, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died within days, aged thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 特贈檢校太保、大同軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was specially posthumously granted Grand Guardian and military governor of Datong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Guardian and military governor of Datong Army.

sentences.zh: 子知節。

translations.literal: His son was Zhijie.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhijie.

sentences.zh: 子 知節

translations.literal: Son: Zhijie
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zhijie

sentences.zh: 知節，字子元，幼孤。

translations.literal: Zhijie, style name Ziyuan, lost his father while young.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie, courtesy name Ziyuan, was orphaned young.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，以蔭補供奉官，賜今名。

translations.literal: In Taizong's time he entered office by hereditary privilege as a palace attendant and was given his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong he entered office by hereditary privilege as a palace attendant and received his present name.

sentences.zh: 年十八，監彭州兵，以嚴蒞眾，眾憚之如老將。

translations.literal: At eighteen he supervised the troops of Peng Prefecture; he kept discipline so strictly that the men feared him like a veteran commander.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he supervised Peng Prefecture troops; his stern discipline made the men fear him like a veteran commander.

sentences.zh: 又監潭州兵，時何承矩為守，頗以文雅飾吏治，知節慕之，因折節讀書。

translations.literal: He also supervised Tan Prefecture troops; He Chengjue was prefect there and rather adorned his administration with literary polish; Zhijie admired him and therefore applied himself to reading.
translations.idiomatic: He later supervised Tan Prefecture troops while He Chengjue, the prefect, cultivated a literary style of governance; Zhijie admired him and took up reading.

sentences.zh: 雍熙間，護兵博州，契丹入邊，敗我師於君子館。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he guarded troops at Bo Prefecture; the Khitan crossed the border and defeated our army at Junzi Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he guarded troops at Bo Prefecture when the Khitan crossed the border and routed the Song army at Junzi Lodge.

sentences.zh: 先是，知節完城繕甲，儲積芻粟，吏民以為生事。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhijie had repaired the walls, readied armor, and stored fodder and grain; officials and people thought he was making trouble for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie had already repaired the walls, readied armor, and stored fodder; locals thought he was making unnecessary trouble.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹果至，以有備，引去。

translations.literal: When the Khitan indeed came, they found the place prepared and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan arrived, they found the city prepared and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 徙知定遠軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Dingyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Dingyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 時議調河南十三州之民輸餉，河北轉運使樊知古適至軍議事，知節曰：「軍少粟多，簸其紅腐，尚當得十之六七。」

translations.literal: At the time it was proposed to mobilize the people of thirteen Henan prefectures to transport supplies; Hebei transport commissioner Fan Zhigu happened to come to the army for consultation. Zhijie said: "The army is small and grain abundant; winnow the rotten red grain and you should still get six or seven tenths."
translations.idiomatic: Officials proposed drafting thirteen Henan prefectures to haul supplies; when Hebei transport commissioner Fan Zhigu came to consult, Zhijie said, "We have little army and much grain; winnow the rotten stock and six or seven tenths should still be usable."

sentences.zh: 知古從之，果獲粟五十萬斛，分給諸屯，遂省河南之役。

translations.literal: Zhigu followed his advice and indeed obtained five hundred thousand hu of grain, distributed it to the garrisons, and thus spared Henan its labor levy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu agreed and obtained five hundred thousand hu, distributed it to the camps, and spared Henan the draft.

sentences.zh: 時部民入保避寇，卒有盜婦女首飾者，護軍止笞遣之。

translations.literal: At the time local people entered the fort to escape raiders; a soldier stole a woman's hair ornaments; the guard officer merely flogged and released him.
translations.idiomatic: When locals took refuge in the fort, a soldier stole a woman's hair ornaments; the guard officer only flogged and released him.

sentences.zh: 知節曰：「民避外患而來，反罹內寇，此而可恕，何以肅下？」

translations.literal: Zhijie said: "The people flee external danger only to suffer internal robbery—if this can be forgiven, how can subordinates be kept in awe?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie said, "People flee outside danger only to meet robbery inside—if this is forgivable, how can discipline be kept?"

sentences.zh: 即命斬之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the man beheaded at once.

sentences.zh: 知深、慶二州，遷西京作坊使。

translations.literal: He governed Zhi and Qing prefectures and was transferred to director of the Western Capital Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Zhi and Qing prefectures, then became director of the Western Capital Workshops.

sentences.zh: 旋知梓州。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 李順之叛，詔與王繼恩同討賊。

translations.literal: When Li Shun rebelled, an edict ordered him and Wang Jien to suppress the rebels together.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun rebelled, he and Wang Jien were ordered to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 繼恩恃勢自任，惡知節不附己，遣守彭州，付以羸兵三百，彭之舊卒，悉召還成都。

translations.literal: Jien relied on his influence and acted on his own; he disliked Zhijie for not siding with him, sent him to guard Peng Prefecture, and gave him only three hundred weak troops—all Peng's old soldiers were recalled to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jien was arrogant and resented Zhijie's independence; he posted Zhijie at Peng Prefecture with only three hundred weak troops and recalled all Peng's veterans to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 知節累請益兵，不從。

translations.literal: Zhijie repeatedly requested reinforcements but was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie repeatedly asked for reinforcements and was refused.

sentences.zh: 賊眾十萬攻城，知節力戰，自晨抵晡，士多死，慨然歎曰：「死賊手，非壯夫也。」

translations.literal: Rebel forces a hundred thousand strong attacked the city; Zhijie fought hard from morning till late afternoon; many soldiers died. He sighed and said: "To die at the hands of bandits is no deed for a true man."
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand rebels besieged the city; Zhijie fought from morning till late afternoon and lost many men. He sighed, "To die at bandit hands is no death for a true man."

sentences.zh: 即橫槊潰圍出，遲明，援兵至，復鼓噪入，賊遂潰去。

translations.literal: He then broke through the encirclement with spear leveled; by dawn relief arrived, and he again charged in with drum and shout; the rebels fled.
translations.idiomatic: He broke out with leveled spear; at dawn relief arrived and he charged back in with drum and shout, and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而歎曰：「賊眾我寡，知節不易當也。」

translations.literal: Taizong heard of it and sighed: "The rebels were many and we were few—Zhijie was not easy to withstand."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong heard and sighed, "Rebels many, defenders few—Zhijie was not easy to beat."

sentences.zh: 授益州鈐轄，加益、漢九州都巡檢使，遷內園使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Baoxin Army controller of Zizhou, additionally made inspector-general of nine prefectures including Yi and Han, and transferred to inner-garden commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Baoxin Army controller of Zizhou, additionally inspector-general of nine prefectures including Yi and Han, and promoted to inner-garden commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會韓景祐帳下劉旰脅牙兵為亂，連下州縣，眾逾二千，知節領兵三百，追至蜀州，與戰，旰走邛州。

translations.literal: When Han Jingyou's follower Liu Gan coerced the guard troops into revolt, successively taking prefectures and counties with a force exceeding two thousand, Zhijie led three hundred men, pursued to Shu Prefecture, fought, and Gan fled to Qiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jingyou's follower Liu Gan forced the guard into revolt and seized prefectures with more than two thousand men, Zhijie led three hundred troops, pursued him to Shu Prefecture, fought, and drove Gan toward Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知節曰：「賊破邛州，必乘勝渡江薄我，既息而後戰，官軍雖倍，制之亦勞，不如乘其弊急擊之，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: Zhijie said: "If the rebels take Qiong Prefecture they will surely cross the river in victory to press us; if we rest and then fight, even twice our numbers will find it hard to control them—it is better to strike their exhaustion at once and break them."
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie said, "If the rebels take Qiong they will cross the river in triumph to press us; rest first and even double our numbers will struggle to stop them—strike their exhaustion now and we can break them."

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: He therefore marched.
translations.idiomatic: He marched at once.

sentences.zh: 次方井鎮，與旰遇，殺之無噍類。

translations.literal: At Fangjing Market he met Gan and killed every last man.
translations.idiomatic: At Fangjing Market he met Gan and slaughtered every last man.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，領登州刺史、知秦州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was made prefect of Deng Prefecture and governor of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xianping he was made prefect of Deng and governor of Qin.

sentences.zh: 州嘗質羌酋支屬餘二十人，逾二紀矣。

translations.literal: The prefecture had long held twenty-odd hostages from Qiang chieftains—more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture still held more than twenty Qiang chieftains' kin as hostages, kept for over twenty years.

sentences.zh: 知節曰：「羌亦人爾，豈不懷歸？」

translations.literal: Zhijie said: "The Qiang too are human—how could they not long to return home?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie said, "The Qiang are people too—would they not long for home?"

sentences.zh: 悉遣之。

translations.literal: He sent them all back.
translations.idiomatic: He sent them all home.

sentences.zh: 羌人感之，訖終，更不犯塞。

translations.literal: The Qiang were moved by this; to the end of his tenure they never again raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang were moved; for the rest of his tenure they never raided the frontier again.

sentences.zh: 時州有銀坑，歲久礦竭，課額弗除，主吏破產，償之不足。

translations.literal: At the time the prefecture had a silver mine long exhausted, yet the tax quota was not removed; responsible officials were ruined and could not pay enough.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had a silver mine long exhausted, yet the tax quota remained; officials were ruined trying to pay it.

sentences.zh: 知節請蠲之，章三上，乃允。

translations.literal: Zhijie requested remission; after three memorials it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie petitioned for remission three times before it was granted.

sentences.zh: 遷西上閤門使，知益州兼本路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and made prefect of Yizhou, concurrently transport commissioner of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became Western Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Yizhou, concurrently circuit transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 自乾德後，歲漕蜀物，動逾萬計。

translations.literal: Since Qiande, yearly transport of Shu goods regularly exceeded ten thousand items.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qiande, annual transport of Shu goods regularly exceeded ten thousand loads.

sentences.zh: 時籍富民以部舟運，坐沉覆破產者眾。

translations.literal: At the time wealthy households were registered to crew the boats; many were ruined by sinkings.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households were registered to crew the boats, and many were ruined when cargoes sank.

sentences.zh: 知節請代督以省校而程其漕事，自是蜀人賴以免患。

translations.literal: Zhijie requested that transport officials supervise instead, using clerks to schedule the hauls; from this the people of Shu were spared the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie proposed that transport officials supervise with clerks scheduling hauls, sparing Shu people the burden.

sentences.zh: 徙知延州兼鄜延駐泊部署。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Yan Prefecture, concurrently deployment commissioner of Fuyan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Yan Prefecture, concurrently Fuyan garrison deployment commissioner.

sentences.zh: 邊寇將至，方上元節，遽命張燈啟關，累夕宴樂。

translations.literal: Border raiders were about to arrive just at the Lantern Festival; he immediately ordered lamps hung and the gates opened, feasting several nights running.
translations.idiomatic: Border raiders were approaching at Lantern Festival; he ordered lamps hung, gates opened, and feasts held night after night.

sentences.zh: 寇不測，即引去。

translations.literal: The raiders could not fathom his intent and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders could not fathom his intent and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會鎮州程德玄政事曠弛，徙知節代之。

translations.literal: When Zhen Prefecture's Cheng Dexuan was lax in administration, Zhijie was transferred to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen Prefecture's Cheng Dexuan was lax in office, Zhijie replaced him.

sentences.zh: 詔發澶、魏等六州糧輸定武，時兵交境上，知節曰：「糧之來，是資盜也。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered grain from six prefectures including Cao and Wei transported to Dingwu; troops were then clashing on the border. Zhijie said: "When grain arrives, it only feeds the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered grain from six prefectures including Cao and Wei sent to Dingwu while troops clashed on the border. Zhijie said, "Incoming grain only feeds the enemy."

sentences.zh: 止令於舟車所至收之，寇無所得而遁。

translations.literal: He ordered collection only where boats and carts could reach; the raiders got nothing and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered grain collected only where boats and carts could reach; the raiders got nothing and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 車駕在澶淵，時王超擁兵數十萬屯真定，逗留不進。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Chanyuan, Wang Chao held several hundred thousand troops at Zhending but lingered without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Chanyuan, Wang Chao held several hundred thousand troops at Zhending but lingered without advancing.

sentences.zh: 知節移書誚讓之，超始出兵，猶以中渡無橋為辭。

translations.literal: Zhijie sent a letter rebuking him; Chao finally marched out, still pleading that there was no bridge at Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie wrote to rebuke him; Chao finally marched out, still claiming there was no bridge at Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 知節預命度材，一夕而具。

translations.literal: Zhijie had already ordered materials measured; overnight a bridge was ready.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie had already ordered timber measured; overnight the bridge was ready.

sentences.zh: 景德中，徙知定州，未幾，拜東上閤門使、樞密都承旨，擢拜簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era he was transferred to Ding Prefecture; shortly he was made Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and promoted signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde he was transferred to Ding Prefecture; soon he was made Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and promoted signatory of that bureau.

sentences.zh: 當是時，契丹已盟，中國無事，大臣方言符瑞，而知節每不然之，嘗言「天下雖安，不可忘戰去兵」以為戒。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan had made peace and the realm was untroubled; grand councilors were just then speaking of portents and omens, yet Zhijie always demurred, saying that though the realm was at peace one must not forget war and cast aside arms.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had made peace and the realm was quiet; ministers spoke of portents, but Zhijie always demurred, warning that peace must not mean forgetting war.

sentences.zh: 自陳年齒未衰，五七年間尚可驅策，如邊方有警，願預其行，但得副都部署名及良馬數匹、輕甲一聯足矣。

translations.literal: He stated that though his years were not yet advanced, in five or seven more he could still be driven into service; if the frontier alarmed, he wished to take part—provided only the title of deputy overall deployment, a few good horses, and a set of light armor.
translations.idiomatic: He said his years were not yet spent; in five or seven more he could still serve, and if the frontier alarmed he wished to go—needing only the title of deputy overall deployment, a few good horses, and light armor.

sentences.zh: 上以為然，因命製銅鐵鎖子甲以賜焉。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right and therefore ordered a copper-and-iron mail coat made and bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and had a copper-and-iron mail coat made for him.

sentences.zh: 進宣徽北院使，加兼樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Domestic Service and additionally made vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Domestic Service and additionally vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時王欽若為樞密使，知節薄其為人，遇事敢言，未嘗少屈。

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo was then commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Zhijie looked down on his character and, when matters arose, spoke boldly and never yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo was then military affairs commissioner; Zhijie despised his character and spoke boldly without yielding.

sentences.zh: 每廷議，得其不直，輒面詆之。

translations.literal: Whenever court deliberations found Qinruo in the wrong, he would denounce him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever court debate found Qinruo wrong, he denounced him to his face.

sentences.zh: 時欽若寵顧方隆，知節愈不為下。

translations.literal: Qinruo's favor was then at its height, yet Zhijie became all the less submissive.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo's favor was then at its height, yet Zhijie grew only more defiant.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符七年，出為潁州防禦使、知潞州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu he went out as defense commissioner of Ying Prefecture and governor of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu he left court as defense commissioner of Ying and governor of Lu.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，移知天雄軍，召拜宣徽南院使、知樞密院事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi he was transferred to govern Tianxiong Army and summoned as Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Domestic Service and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianxi he was transferred to Tianxiong Army and summoned as Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Domestic Service and military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞罷，除彰德軍留後、知貝州兼部署。

translations.literal: Ill, he begged to resign and was made military prefect of Zhangde Army, governor of Bei Prefecture, and deployment commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he begged leave and was made military prefect of Zhangde Army, governor of Bei Prefecture, and deployment commissioner.

sentences.zh: 將行，真宗閔其臒瘁，止命歸鎮。

translations.literal: About to depart, Zhenzong, pitying his emaciation, ordered him simply to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: About to depart, Zhenzong, pitying his wasted frame, ordered him simply to return to his command.

sentences.zh: 時上黨、大名之民已爭來迎謁。

translations.literal: By then the people of Shangdang and Daming were already competing to come welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: By then the people of Shangdang and Daming were already rushing to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，諡正惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant with the posthumous title Zhenghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant with the posthumous title Zhenghui ("Correct and Gracious").

sentences.zh: 知節將家子，慷慨以武力智謀自許，又能好書，賓友儒者，所與善厚，必一時豪傑，論事謇謇未嘗有所顧忌，故聞其風者，亦知其為正直云。

translations.literal: Zhijie was born to a military family, generous and self-confident in martial prowess and stratagem, yet also fond of books; he befriended scholars, and those he befriended deeply were always men of the age; in debate he spoke bluntly without regard for consequences—so those who heard of his manner knew him for an upright man.
translations.idiomatic: Born to a military house, Zhijie was generous and confident in arms and strategy, yet also loved books and befriended scholars; those he held close were always leading men of the age, and in debate he spoke bluntly without fear—so all who knew his reputation knew him for an upright man.

sentences.zh: 雷德驤

translations.literal: Lei Dexiang
translations.idiomatic: Lei Dexiang

sentences.zh: 雷德驤，字善行，同州郃陽人。

translations.literal: Lei Dexiang, style name Shanxing, was a man of Heyang in Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Dexiang, courtesy name Shanxing, was from Heyang in Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 周廣順三年舉進士，解褐磁州軍事判官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangshun in Zhou he passed the jinshi examination, entered office as military adjutant of Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangshun in Zhou he passed the jinshi and entered office as military adjutant of Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召為右拾遺，充三司判官，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Reminder and appointed judge of the Three Departments, and was granted crimson robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Right Reminder, made judge of the Three Departments, and granted crimson robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，入受詔均定隨州諸縣民田屋稅，稱為平允。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era he received an edict to equalize household and dwelling taxes in the counties of Sui Prefecture; he was praised as fair and even.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiande era he received an edict to equalize household and dwelling taxes in Sui Prefecture's counties and was praised as fair.

sentences.zh: 宋初，拜殿中侍御史，改屯田員外郎、判大理寺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was made Palace Attendant-in-Waiting and transferred to Field Administration Officer and judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Song he was made Palace Attendant-in-Waiting, then Field Administration Officer and judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 其官屬與堂吏附會宰相趙普，擅增刑名，因上言，欲求見太祖以白其事。

translations.literal: His subordinates and clerks of the hall colluded with Grand Councilor Zhao Pu and arbitrarily added penalties; he therefore submitted a memorial requesting audience with Taizu to report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates and hall clerks colluded with Grand Councilor Zhao Pu and arbitrarily added penalties; he memorialized requesting audience with Taizu to report it.

sentences.zh: 未引對，直詣講武殿奏之，辭氣俱厲。

translations.literal: Before he was granted audience he went straight to the Lecture Hall and reported it; his words and tone were both fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Before audience was granted he went straight to the Lecture Hall and reported it in fierce tones.

sentences.zh: 太祖詰之，德驤對曰：「臣值陛下日旰未食，方震威嚴爾。」

translations.literal: Taizu interrogated him; Dexiang replied: "Your subject came upon Your Majesty still unfed at sunset—hence I was awed by Your Majesty's majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu interrogated him; Dexiang replied, "Your subject found Your Majesty still unfed at sunset—I was awed by Your Majesty's majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，令左右曳出，詔置極典。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered attendants to drag him out and decreed the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry, had him dragged out, and decreed the extreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 俄怒解，黜為商州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Shortly the anger eased and he was demoted to revenue clerk of Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly the anger eased and he was demoted to revenue clerk of Shang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 刺史知德驤舊為省郎，以客禮之。

translations.literal: The prefect knew Dexiang had formerly been a provincial official and treated him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect knew Dexiang had once been a provincial official and treated him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 及奚嶼知州，希宰相旨，至則倨受庭參。

translations.literal: When Xi Yu became prefect, hoping to please the grand councilor, he received Dexiang's court visit with arrogant haughtiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Yu became prefect, hoping to please the grand councilor, he received Dexiang's court visit with arrogant contempt.

sentences.zh: 德驤不能堪，出怨言，嶼銜之。

translations.literal: Dexiang could not bear it and spoke resentfully; Yu harbored a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiang could not bear it and spoke resentfully; Yu nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 適有言德驤至郡為文訕上者，嶼召德驤與語，潛遣吏紿其家人取得之，即械繫德驤，具狀以聞。

translations.literal: It happened that someone reported Dexiang had written a piece satirizing the emperor at the prefecture; Yu summoned Dexiang to talk and secretly sent an official to trick his family into handing it over; he then shackled Dexiang and submitted a full report.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported Dexiang had written a piece satirizing the emperor; Yu summoned him, secretly tricked his family into surrendering the text, shackled Dexiang, and submitted a full report.

sentences.zh: 太祖貸其罪，削籍徙靈武。

translations.literal: Taizu pardoned his crime, struck him from the rolls, and exiled him to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu pardoned his life, struck him from the rolls, and exiled him to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 數年，其子有鄰擊登聞鼓，訴中書不法事，趙普由是出鎮河陽。

translations.literal: Several years later his son Youlin struck the Denunciation Drum and sued the Secretariat for illegal conduct; Zhao Pu was therefore sent out to govern Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later his son Youlin struck the Denunciation Drum and sued the Secretariat for illegal conduct; Zhao Pu was therefore sent to govern Heyang.

sentences.zh: 召德驤為秘書丞，俄分判御史臺三院事，又兼判吏部南曹。

translations.literal: Dexiang was summoned as Secretariat Director and shortly divided duties among the three bureaus of the Censorate, additionally judging the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiang was summoned as Secretariat Director, shortly divided duties among the three Censorate bureaus, and additionally judged the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 開寶七年，同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaibao he jointly supervised the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaibao he jointly supervised the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，以德驤為吳越國告哀使。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, Dexiang was made envoy to announce mourning to the state of Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu died, Dexiang was made envoy to announce mourning to Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 還，遷戶部員外郎兼御史知雜事，改職方員外郎，充陝西、河北轉運使。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted Revenue Officer and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, transferred to Bureau Officer, and made transport commissioner of Shaanxi and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was promoted Revenue Officer and Censor-in-Chief, transferred to Bureau Officer, and made transport commissioner of Shaanxi and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 歷禮部、戶部郎中，入為度支判官。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director of Rites and Director of Revenue, then entered office as judge of the Revenue Office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of Rites and Director of Revenue, then entered office as judge of the Revenue Office.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，車駕征太原，為太原西路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, when the imperial carriage marched on Taiyuan, he was made transport commissioner of the Taiyuan Western Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, when the emperor marched on Taiyuan, he was made transport commissioner of the Taiyuan Western Route.

sentences.zh: 六年，同知京朝官考課，俄遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he jointly supervised the capital-official performance review and shortly was promoted Director of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he jointly supervised the capital-official performance review and was soon promoted Director of War.

sentences.zh: 七年，以公累降本曹員外郎、出知懷州，未幾，復舊官，又命為兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, for official misconduct he was demoted to Bureau Officer of his own ministry and sent out as prefect of Huai Prefecture; before long he recovered his old rank and was again made transport commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, for official misconduct he was demoted and sent out as prefect of Huai; before long he recovered his rank and was again made transport commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 其子殿中丞有終亦為淮南轉運使，父子同日受詔，搢紳榮之。

translations.literal: His son Palace Attendant Youzhong was also made Huainan transport commissioner; father and son received edicts the same day—the gentry counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youzhong was also made Huainan transport commissioner; father and son received edicts the same day—an honor the gentry noted.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was promoted Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，征歸朝，同知京朝官考課，初，帝謂宰相曰：「朕前日閱班籍，擇官為河北轉運使，所患不能周知群臣履行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was recalled and jointly supervised the capital-official performance review. Earlier the emperor had told the grand councilors: "The other day I reviewed the roster to choose officials for Hebei transport commissioner; what I feared was not knowing the conduct of the officials thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he was recalled to jointly supervise the capital-official performance review. Earlier the emperor had told grand councilors, "When I reviewed the roster to choose a Hebei transport commissioner, I feared not knowing officials' conduct thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 自今令德驤錄京朝官履歷功過之狀引對，既得漸識群臣，擇才委任，且使有官政者樂於召對，負瑕累者恥於顧問，可以為懲勸矣。」

translations.literal: From now on let Dexiang record capital officials' careers, merits, and faults and bring them for audience—thus I may gradually know the officials, choose talent and assign posts, and also make those with good records glad to be summoned and those with blemishes ashamed to be questioned; this can serve as warning and encouragement."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth let Dexiang record capital officials' careers, merits, and faults and bring them for audience—so I may gradually know the officials, choose talent wisely, make the capable glad to be summoned, and the blemished ashamed to be questioned; this can warn and encourage."

sentences.zh: 端拱初，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was promoted Vice Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong he was promoted Vice Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 會趙普再入相，宣制之日，德驤方立班，不覺墜笏，遽上疏，乞歸田里。

translations.literal: When Zhao Pu again entered the chancellorship, on the day the edict was promulgated Dexiang was standing in court formation and, without noticing, dropped his tablet; he immediately submitted a memorial begging to return to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Pu again became chancellor, on the day the edict was read Dexiang, standing in court formation, dropped his tablet without noticing and immediately memorialized begging to retire.

sentences.zh: 太宗召見，安諭之，賜白金三千兩，罷知考課，止以本官奉朝請。

translations.literal: Taizong summoned him, reassured him, granted three thousand taels of white gold, removed him from supervising the performance review, and retained him only in his original rank at court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned him, reassured him, granted three thousand taels of white gold, removed him from supervising performance reviews, and kept him at court in his original rank.

sentences.zh: 會議事尚書省，乘酒叱起居員外郎鄭構為盜，御史奏劾，下御史臺案問，具伏，帝止令罰月奉而釋之。

translations.literal: When deliberating affairs at the Ministry of Revenue he, drunk, shouted at Attendance Officer Zheng Gou that he was a thief; the censor memorialized impeachment; he was handed to the Censorate for investigation, confessed fully, and the emperor merely fined one month's salary and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberating at the Ministry of Revenue while drunk, he shouted at Attendance Officer Zheng Gou that he was a thief; impeached and investigated, he confessed; the emperor merely fined one month's salary and released him.

sentences.zh: 訖趙普出守西洛，帝終保全之。

translations.literal: When Zhao Pu finally went out to guard the Western Capital, the emperor still protected Dexiang to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Pu finally went out to guard the Western Capital, the emperor still protected Dexiang to the end.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，為其婿如京副使衛濯訟有鄰子秘書省校書郎孝先內亂，帝素憐德驤，恐暴揚其醜，不以孝先屬吏，止除名配均州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, his son-in-law Vice Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service Wei Zhuo sued Youlin's son Secretariat Proofreader Xiaoxian for incest; the emperor had long pitied Dexiang and, fearing exposure of family shame, did not hand Xiaoxian to the judicial authorities but merely struck his name and assigned him to Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua his son-in-law Wei Zhuo sued Youlin's son Xiaoxian for incest; the emperor, pitying Dexiang and fearing family shame exposed, did not hand Xiaoxian to the courts but merely struck his name and assigned him to Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德驤坐失教，責授感德軍行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Dexiang was punished for failure to teach and was made acting marshal of Gandé Army.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiang was punished for failure to teach and was made acting marshal of Gandé Army.

sentences.zh: 並其子少府少監有終責授衡州團練副使。

translations.literal: Together with his son Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service Youzhong he was punished and made regimental deputy commissioner of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his son Youzhong he was punished and made regimental deputy commissioner of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德驤因慚憤成疾，三年，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: Dexiang, shamed and angry, fell ill; in the third year he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiang, shamed and angry, fell ill; in the third year he died, aged seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 有終為三司鹽鐵副使，表乞追復舊官，從之。

translations.literal: Youzhong, as Vice Commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly under the Three Departments, memorialized begging restoration of his father's old rank; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong, as Salt and Iron Vice Commissioner under the Three Departments, memorialized begging restoration of his father's old rank; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 德驤無文采，頗以強直自任，性褊躁，多忤物，不為士大夫所與。

translations.literal: Dexiang had no literary polish; he rather relied on forceful uprightness, was narrow and quick-tempered, often gave offense, and was not accepted by the literati.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiang lacked literary polish, relied on blunt uprightness, was narrow and quick-tempered, often gave offense, and was not accepted by literati.

sentences.zh: 子 有鄰

translations.literal: Son: Youlin
translations.idiomatic: Son: Youlin

sentences.zh: 有鄰，開寶中，舉進士不第。

translations.literal: Youlin, in the Kaibao era, took the jinshi examination and failed.
translations.idiomatic: Youlin took the jinshi in the Kaibao era and failed.

sentences.zh: 其父既竄靈武，意宰相趙普擠抑之。

translations.literal: After his father was exiled to Lingwu, he believed Grand Councilor Zhao Pu had squeezed him out.
translations.idiomatic: After his father was exiled to Lingwu, he believed Grand Councilor Zhao Pu had forced him out.

sentences.zh: 時堂後吏胡讚、李可度在職歲久，或稱其請託受賕，而秘書丞王洞與德驤同年登第，有鄰每造謁洞，洞多以家事委之。

translations.literal: At the time Hall Attendants Hu Zan and Li Kedou had long held office; some said they solicited favors and took bribes; Secretariat Director Wang Dong had passed the examinations the same year as Dexiang, and Youlin often visited Dong, who often entrusted him with household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hall Attendants Hu Zan and Li Kedou had long held office; some said they solicited favors and took bribes; Secretariat Director Wang Dong had passed the examinations the same year as Dexiang, and Youlin often visited Dong, who often entrusted him with household affairs.

sentences.zh: 一日，洞令有鄰市白金半鋌，因曰：「此令吾子知，要與胡將軍。」

translations.literal: One day Dong had Youlin buy half a ingot of white gold and said: "Let my son know of this—it is for General Hu."
translations.idiomatic: One day Dong had Youlin buy half an ingot of white gold and said, "Let my son know—this is for General Hu."

sentences.zh: 蓋謂讚也。

translations.literal: This referred to Zan.
translations.idiomatic: He meant Zan.

sentences.zh: 時又有詔，應攝官三任解由全者許投牒有司，即得召試錄用。

translations.literal: At the time there was also an edict that provisional officials who completed three terms with full certificates of release might submit petitions to the relevant office and be summoned for examination and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also allowed provisional officials who completed three terms with full release certificates to petition the relevant office and be summoned for examination and appointment.

sentences.zh: 有鄰素與前攝上蔡主簿劉偉交遊，知偉雖嘗三攝，而一任失其解由，偉造偽印，令其兄前進士侁書寫之，因是得試送銓。

translations.literal: Youlin had long been friendly with former provisional chief clerk of Shangcai Liu Wei and knew that though Wei had served three provisional terms, one term lacked its release certificate; Wei forged a seal and had his elder brother, former jinshi Liu Xian, write it out, and thus entered examination and was sent to the Board of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Youlin was friendly with former provisional chief clerk Liu Wei, who though having served three provisional terms lacked one release certificate; Wei forged a seal and had his jinshi brother Xian write it, entered examination, and was sent to the Board of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 遂具章告其事，並下御史府按鞫。

translations.literal: Youlin then submitted a full memorial reporting these matters, and all were handed to the Censorate for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Youlin then submitted a full memorial reporting these matters, and all were handed to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 有鄰出入讚家，故其事多實。

translations.literal: Youlin went in and out of Zan's house, so the matters were largely substantiated.
translations.idiomatic: Youlin frequented Zan's house, so the charges were largely substantiated.

sentences.zh: 獄具，偉坐棄市，洞等並決杖除名，讚、可度仍籍其家。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, Wei was executed in the marketplace; Dong and the others were all flogged and struck from the rolls; Zan and Kedou still had their households registered.
translations.idiomatic: When the case closed, Wei was executed; Dong and others were flogged and struck from the rolls; Zan and Kedou still had their households registered.

sentences.zh: 有鄰授秘書省正字，賜公服靴笏、銀鞍勒馬、絹百匹，自是累上疏密告人陰事。

translations.literal: Youlin was appointed Secretariat Proofreader, granted official robes, boots, tablet, silver saddle and bridle, horse, and a hundred bolts of silk; from this he repeatedly submitted secret memorials reporting others' private affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Youlin was appointed Secretariat Proofreader, granted official robes, boots, tablet, silver saddle, horse, and a hundred bolts of silk; thereafter he repeatedly submitted secret memorials reporting private affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄被病，白晝見偉入室，以杖箠其背。

translations.literal: Shortly he fell ill; in broad daylight he saw Wei enter the room and beat his back with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he fell ill; in broad daylight he saw Wei enter the room and beat his back with a staff.

sentences.zh: 有鄰號呼聞於外，數日而死。

translations.literal: Youlin cried out loud enough to be heard outside; within days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Youlin cried out loud enough to be heard outside; within days he died.

sentences.zh: 賜德驤錢十萬，以給喪事。

translations.literal: Dexiang was granted one hundred thousand cash for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiang was granted one hundred thousand cash for funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 子 有終

translations.literal: Son: Youzhong
translations.idiomatic: Son: Youzhong

sentences.zh: 有終，字道成，幼聰敏，以蔭補漢州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Youzhong, style name Daocheng, was clever from youth and entered office by hereditary privilege as revenue clerk of Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong, courtesy name Daocheng, was clever from youth and entered office by hereditary privilege as revenue clerk of Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時侯陟典選，木強難犯，選人聽署於庭，無敢嘩者。

translations.literal: At the time Hou Zhi controlled appointments; he was stern and hard to cross; candidates signed in the courtyard and none dared make noise.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhi controlled appointments; stern and hard to cross, he had candidates sign in the courtyard and none dared make noise.

sentences.zh: 有終獨抗言，願為大郡治獄掾，陟叱之曰：「年未三十，安可任此官？」

translations.literal: Youzhong alone spoke up boldly, wishing to serve as judicial aide in a large prefecture; Zhi shouted at him: "Not yet thirty—how can you hold such an office?"
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong alone spoke boldly, wishing to serve as judicial aide in a large prefecture; Zhi shouted, "Not yet thirty—how can you hold such an office?"

sentences.zh: 有終不為沮。

translations.literal: Youzhong was not discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong was not discouraged.

sentences.zh: 署萊蕪尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Laiwu county captain.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Laiwu county captain.

sentences.zh: 知監、左拾遺劉祺以有終年少，頗易之。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Directorate of Monopolies and Left Reminder Liu Qi thought Youzhong young and rather looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Directorate of Monopolies Liu Qi thought Youzhong young and looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 有終發其奸贓，祺坐罪杖流海島，以有終代知監事。

translations.literal: Youzhong exposed his corruption; Qi was punished by flogging and exile to a sea island, and Youzhong replaced him as acting supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong exposed his corruption; Qi was flogged and exiled to a sea island, and Youzhong replaced him as acting supervisor.

sentences.zh: 先是，三司補吏為冶官，率以貲進，多恣橫。

translations.literal: Earlier the Three Departments supplemented clerks as foundry officials, who generally bought their posts with wealth and mostly acted wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Three Departments supplemented clerks as foundry officials, who generally bought posts with wealth and acted wantonly.

sentences.zh: 至是，受署者憚有終，率多避免。

translations.literal: From this those appointed feared Youzhong and mostly avoided the post.
translations.idiomatic: From this appointees feared Youzhong and mostly avoided the post.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，聞其名，遣內侍伍守忠同掌監事，且察其治跡。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded he heard his name and dispatched Inner Attendant Wu Shouzhong to jointly supervise the directorate and observe his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong acceded he heard Youzhong's name and dispatched Inner Attendant Wu Shouzhong to jointly supervise the directorate and observe his conduct.

sentences.zh: 守忠至裁周月，即還奏有終強濟之狀，亟詔為大理寺丞。

translations.literal: Shouzhong had been there barely a month when he returned and reported Youzhong's forceful efficiency; an urgent edict made him Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong returned within a month reporting Youzhong's forceful efficiency; an urgent edict made him Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 會德驤任陝西轉運，奏為解州通判，特許德驤不巡察是州。

translations.literal: When Dexiang served as Shaanxi transport commissioner he memorialized him as vice prefect of Jie Prefecture, specially permitting Dexiang not to inspect that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Dexiang served as Shaanxi transport commissioner he memorialized Youzhong as vice prefect of Jie Prefecture, specially exempting that prefecture from Dexiang's inspection.

sentences.zh: 有終入奏鹽池利害，改贊善大夫，令還權知軍事，省通判。

translations.literal: Youzhong entered court to report on the salt ponds' advantages and disadvantages; he was changed to Senior Supporter and ordered back to hold military affairs in place of the vice prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong entered court to report on the salt ponds; he was changed to Senior Supporter and ordered back to hold military affairs without a vice prefect.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，遷殿中丞、知密州，徙淮南轉運副使，賜緋魚，改太常博士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted Palace Attendant and made prefect of Mi Prefecture, transferred to deputy Huainan transport commissioner, granted crimson robe and fish tally, and changed to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted Palace Attendant and prefect of Mi Prefecture, transferred to deputy Huainan transport commissioner, granted crimson robe and fish tally, and made Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時德驤主漕兩浙，往往省於境上，時人榮之。

translations.literal: At the time Dexiang supervised transport in the Two Zhe circuits and often saved effort at the border; contemporaries counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiang then supervised transport in the Two Zhe circuits and often saved effort at the border—contemporaries counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，王師北征，命為蔚州飛狐路隨軍轉運使。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, when the imperial army marched north, he was made Feihu Route army transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era, when the imperial army marched north, he was made Feihu Route army transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入為鹽鐵判官，歷戶部、度支副使，賜金紫，出知昇州。

translations.literal: He entered office as Salt and Iron judge, served successively as Vice Director of Revenue and Vice Director of the Revenue Office, was granted gold and purple, and went out as prefect of Sheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as Salt and Iron judge, rose through vice directorships of Revenue and the Revenue Office, was granted gold and purple, and went out as prefect of Sheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，就遷少府少監、知廣州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was promoted on the spot to Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service and prefect of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chunhua he was promoted on the spot to Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service and prefect of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年，女弟婿衛濯訟其家法不謹，有終坐親累，責授衡州團練副使，奪章服。

translations.literal: In the second year his younger sister's husband Wei Zhuo sued his household for lax discipline; Youzhong was punished as kin, made regimental deputy commissioner of Heng Prefecture, and stripped of his insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year his brother-in-law Wei Zhuo sued his household for lax discipline; Youzhong was punished as kin, made regimental deputy commissioner of Heng Prefecture, and stripped of insignia.

sentences.zh: 俄丁外艱，行及許田，召歸，入對，賜錢八十萬，起為都官員外郎，歷度支、鹽鐵副使，復金紫。

translations.literal: Shortly he mourned his father; on the road at Xutian he was recalled, entered audience, was granted eight hundred thousand cash, and restored as Director of the Department of State Affairs, then Vice Director of Revenue and Salt and Iron, and again granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he mourned his father; recalled at Xutian, he entered audience, was granted eight hundred thousand cash, restored as Director of the Department of State Affairs, then Vice Director of Revenue and Salt and Iron, and again granted gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 時以江南、嶺外茶鹽價不一，細民冒禁私販，多陷重辟。

translations.literal: At the time tea and salt prices differed between Jiangnan, Lingwai, and other regions; common people violated bans and smuggled privately, often falling into heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Tea and salt prices differed between Jiangnan, Lingwai, and other regions; commoners violated bans and smuggled, often facing heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 詔有終領江淮、兩浙、荊湖、福建、廣南路茶鹽制置使，就出鹽產茶之地，以便宜裁制。

translations.literal: An edict made Youzhong Commissioner for Tea and Salt in the circuits of Jiang-Huai, Two Zhe, Jing-Hu, Fujian, and Guangnan, with discretionary authority at the places of salt production and tea cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Youzhong Commissioner for Tea and Salt across Jiang-Huai, Two Zhe, Jing-Hu, Fujian, and Guangnan, with discretionary authority at salt and tea sources.

sentences.zh: 使還，改工部郎中、知大名府，不逾月，復為少府少監，徙知江陵。

translations.literal: On his return he was changed to Director of War and prefect of Daming Prefecture; within a month he was again Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service and transferred to prefect of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made Director of War and prefect of Daming; within a month he was again Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service and transferred to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 李順之亂，王師西征，命與裴莊為峽路隨軍轉運使、同知兵馬事。

translations.literal: When Li Shun rebelled and the imperial army marched west, he was ordered with Pei Zhuang to serve as Xialu Route army transport commissioner and jointly supervise military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun rebelled and the imperial army marched west, he and Pei Zhuang were made Xialu Route army transport commissioners and jointly supervised military affairs.

sentences.zh: 調發兵食，規畫戎事，皆有節制。

translations.literal: Mobilizing troops and grain and planning military affairs, all were regulated with restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilizing troops and grain and planning military affairs, all were handled with restraint.

sentences.zh: 師行至峽中，遇盜格鬥，眾渴乏，會天雨，軍士以兜牟承水飲之，且行且戰，進至廣安軍，軍壘瀕江，三面樹柵。

translations.literal: When the army reached the gorges it met bandits in combat; the troops were thirsty and exhausted; rain happened to fall and soldiers drank water caught in their helmets as they marched and fought, advancing to Guang'an Army; the camp lay beside the river with palisades on three sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the gorges the army met bandits; thirsty and exhausted, the troops caught rain in their helmets and drank as they fought forward to Guang'an Army, where the camp lay beside the river with palisades on three sides.

sentences.zh: 會夜陰晦，賊眾奄至，鼓噪舉火，士伍恐懼，有終安坐櫛髮自若。

translations.literal: That night the sky was dark; rebel forces suddenly arrived, shouting and raising torches; the troops were terrified, yet Youzhong sat calmly combing his hair.
translations.idiomatic: That night the sky was dark; rebels suddenly arrived with shouts and torches; the troops panicked, yet Youzhong sat calmly combing his hair.

sentences.zh: 賊圍既合，有終引奇兵出其後擊之，賊眾驚擾，赴水死者無算。

translations.literal: Once the rebel encirclement closed, Youzhong led picked troops out behind them to strike; the rebel host panicked and very many drowned fleeing into the water.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel encirclement closed, Youzhong led picked troops out behind them; the rebels panicked and very many drowned fleeing into the water.

sentences.zh: 就拜右諫議大夫、知益州。

translations.literal: He was promoted on the spot to Right Remonstrator and made prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted on the spot to Right Remonstrator and made prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 次簡州，寓佛舍，度賊必至，命左右重閉，召土人嚴更警備，初夕，間道而出。

translations.literal: At Jian Prefecture he lodged in a Buddhist monastery; judging the rebels would surely come, he ordered attendants to seal the doors heavily, summoned locals to tighten the watch, and at first dusk slipped out by a hidden path.
translations.idiomatic: At Jian Prefecture he lodged in a monastery; expecting rebels, he sealed the doors, summoned locals to tighten the watch, and at first dusk slipped out by a hidden path.

sentences.zh: 賊圍守數重，及壞寺入，惟擊柝者在焉。

translations.literal: Rebel encirclement was several layers deep; when they broke into the ruined monastery only the night-watch striker remained.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel encirclement was several layers deep; when they broke into the ruined monastery only the night-watch striker remained.

sentences.zh: 俄兼同招安使。

translations.literal: Shortly he was additionally made Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was additionally made Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊平，改知許州。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was changed to prefect of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified he was changed to prefect of Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，改給事中、知并州。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to Senior Supporter and made prefect of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was changed to Senior Supporter and made prefect of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，加工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded he was additionally made Vice Director of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded he was additionally made Vice Director of War.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，代還，知審刑院，俄授戶部使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he returned on replacement and governed the Court of Judicial Review; shortly he was made Revenue Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping he returned and governed the Court of Judicial Review; shortly he was made Revenue Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，將巡師大名，遣有終乘驛先詣澶州督納糧草。

translations.literal: In the third year, about to review troops at Daming, he dispatched Youzhong by post relay first to Cao Prefecture to supervise grain and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, about to review troops at Daming, he dispatched Youzhong by relay first to Cao Prefecture to supervise grain and fodder.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，次德清軍，會益州奏至，神衛戍卒以正旦竊發，害兵馬鈐轄符昭壽，擁都虞候王均為亂，逐知州牛冕。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned and halted at Deqing Army, a report arrived from Yizhou: Divine Guard garrison troops had mutinied on New Year's Day, killed military controller Fu Zhaoshou, installed Chief Adjutant Wang Jun as leader, and expelled Prefect Niu Mian.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned and halted at Deqing Army, a report arrived from Yizhou: Divine Guard garrison troops mutinied on New Year's Day, killed military controller Fu Zhaoshou, made Chief Adjutant Wang Jun leader, and expelled Prefect Niu Mian.

sentences.zh: 即日，拜有終瀘州觀察使、知益州兼川峽兩路招安捉賊事。

translations.literal: That same day Youzhong was made Observer of Lu Prefecture and Prefect of Yizhou, concurrently Pacification-and-Capture Commissioner for the Two Chuan Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Youzhong was made Observer of Lu Prefecture and Prefect of Yizhou, concurrently Pacification-and-Capture Commissioner for the Two Chuan Circuits.

sentences.zh: 御廚使李惠、洛苑使石普、供備庫副使李守倫並為招安巡檢使，給步騎八千，命往招討。

translations.literal: Imperial Kitchen Commissioner Li Hui, Luoyuan Commissioner Shi Pu, and Supply Repository Deputy Commissioner Li Shoulun were all made Pacification-and-Inspection Commissioners; eight thousand infantry and cavalry were given them and they were ordered to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Kitchen Commissioner Li Hui, Luoyuan Commissioner Shi Pu, and Supply Repository Deputy Commissioner Li Shoulun were all made Pacification-and-Inspection Commissioners; eight thousand infantry and cavalry were given them to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 又以洺州團練使上官正為東川都鈐轄，西京作坊使李繼昌為峽路都鈐轄，崇儀副使高繼勳、王阮並為益州駐泊都監，供奉官、閤門祗候孫正辭為諸州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Further, Luozhou Regimental Commissioner Shangguan Zheng was made Eastern Chuan Controller; Western Capital Workshop Commissioner Li Jichang was made Xialu Route Controller; Honored Ceremonial Deputy Commissioners Gao Jixun and Wang Ruan were both made Yizhou Garrison Supervisors; Attendant Official and Gate Aide Sun Zhengci was made Inspector-General of the Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Zheng was made Eastern Chuan Controller; Li Jichang Xialu Route Controller; Gao Jixun and Wang Ruan Yizhou Garrison Supervisors; Sun Zhengci Inspector-General of the Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 正月三日，均率眾陷漢州，進攻綿州，旬日不能下，趣劍門。

translations.literal: On the third day of the first month Jun led his host to take Han Prefecture, attacked Mian Prefecture, and after ten days could not take it; he hastened toward Jianmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the first month Jun took Han Prefecture, attacked Mian Prefecture, and after ten days could not take it; he hastened toward Jianmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 先是，知劍州、秘書丞李士衡度寇必至，城不能守，悉徙官帑保劍門，焚其倉廩，及署榜招軍卒之流逸者，得數千人。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Shiheng, prefect of Jian Prefecture and Secretariat Proofreader, judged the bandits would surely come and the city could not be held; he moved all official stores to secure Jianmen Pass, burned the granaries, and posted notices recruiting scattered soldiers, obtaining several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Shiheng, prefect of Jian and Secretariat Proofreader, judged the bandits would come and the city could not be held; he moved official stores to Jianmen Pass, burned the granaries, and recruited scattered soldiers, obtaining several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 已而賊果至，士衡與劍門都監、左藏庫副使裴臻逆擊之。

translations.literal: When the bandits indeed came, Shiheng and Jianmen Garrison Supervisor Pei Zhen counterattacked them.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came, Shiheng and Jianmen Garrison Supervisor Pei Zhen counterattacked.

sentences.zh: 時風雪連日，均眾無所掠，唯食敗糟，臻與戰，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Snow and wind lasted days; Jun's host had nothing to plunder and ate only spoiled lees; Zhen fought them and beheaded several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Snow and wind lasted days; Jun's host had nothing to plunder and ate spoiled lees; Zhen fought and beheaded several thousand.

sentences.zh: 賊眾疲劇宵遁，還保益州。

translations.literal: The rebel host, exhausted, fled by night and withdrew to hold Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, exhausted, fled by night back to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 士衡即馳騎入奏，上嘉之，拜士衡度支員外郎，賜緋；

translations.literal: Shiheng immediately galloped in to report; the emperor praised him, made Shiheng Vice Director of the Revenue Office, and granted crimson robe;
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng galloped in to report; the emperor praised him, made Shiheng Vice Director of the Revenue Office, and granted crimson robe;

sentences.zh: 臻崇儀使、領峰州刺史，仍舊職。

translations.literal: Zhen Honored Ceremonial Commissioner and regimental commissioner of Feng Prefecture, retaining his old post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Honored Ceremonial Commissioner and regimental commissioner of Feng Prefecture, retaining his old post.

sentences.zh: 知蜀州、供奉官、閤門祗候楊懷忠聞變，即調鄉丁會十一路巡檢兵，刻期進討。

translations.literal: Yang Huaizhong, Attendant Official and Gate Aide and prefect of Shu Prefecture, on hearing the upheaval immediately mobilized local militia and joined eleven route inspection troops, fixing a date to advance and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huaizhong, Attendant Official, Gate Aide, and prefect of Shu Prefecture, on hearing the upheaval mobilized local militia and joined eleven route inspection troops on a fixed date to advance.

sentences.zh: 蜀民不從賊者相率抗禦，儕伍謂之「清壇眾」。

translations.literal: Shu people who would not follow the rebels resisted in groups; their companies were called the "Pure Altar Host."
translations.idiomatic: Shu people who refused the rebels resisted in groups; their companies were called the "Pure Altar Host."

sentences.zh: 擇「清壇」之魁七十餘人，悉補巡檢將，遣判官高本馳驛以聞。

translations.literal: From the chiefs of the "Pure Altar" host, more than seventy were chosen; all were appointed inspection generals, and Adjunct Official Gao Ben was dispatched by post relay to report it.
translations.idiomatic: More than seventy chiefs of the Pure Altar Host were chosen and made inspection generals; Adjunct Official Gao Ben was sent by relay to report it.

sentences.zh: 十七日，懷忠率眾入益州，焚城北門，至三井橋。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day, Huaizhong led his host into Yizhou, burned the north gate of the city, and reached Sanjing Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth, Huaizhong led his forces into Yizhou, burned the north gate, and reached Sanjing Bridge.

sentences.zh: 時均尚留劍門，與賊將魯麻胡陣於江瀆廟前，自晨至晡，戰數合，懷忠兵勢不敵，退還所部。

translations.literal: At this time Jun was still at Jianmen; he and the bandit general Lu Mahu drew up in battle array before the River God Temple. From morning to late afternoon they fought several rounds; Huaizhong's troops could not match their strength and withdrew to his own command.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was still at Jianmen Pass while Huaizhong fought the bandit general Lu Mahu before the River God Temple from morning till late afternoon in several clashes; outmatched, Huaizhong fell back to his own camp.

sentences.zh: 懷忠部下多李順舊黨，頗貪剽劫，故敗績焉。

translations.literal: Many of Huaizhong's subordinates were old partisans of Li Shun and were rather greedy for plunder and raid—hence the defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Huaizhong's men were former followers of Li Shun and inclined to looting, which accounted for the defeat.

sentences.zh: 懷忠移文嘉、眉七州，調軍士丁男來會。

translations.literal: Huaizhong dispatched official letters to the seven prefectures of Jia and Mei, mobilizing soldiers and adult males to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhong sent dispatches to the seven prefectures around Jia and Mei, calling up soldiers and able-bodied men to join him.

sentences.zh: 二月，再攻益州。

translations.literal: In the second month, he again attacked Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he attacked Yizhou again.

sentences.zh: 時均方遣逆黨趙延順攻邛、蜀，懷忠逆與之戰，賊稍退。

translations.literal: At this time Jun had just sent the rebel partisan Zhao Yanshun to attack Qiong and Shu; Huaizhong went to meet and fight him, and the bandits withdrew somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had sent the rebel Zhao Yanshun against Qiong and Shu; Huaizhong intercepted him and drove the rebels back somewhat.

sentences.zh: 懷忠與轉運使陳緯麾兵由子城南門直入軍資庫，與緯署其庫籥。

translations.literal: Huaizhong and Transport Commissioner Chen Wei led troops through the south gate of the inner city straight into the military supplies storehouse; with Wei he sealed its keys.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhong and Transport Commissioner Chen Wei marched through the inner city's south gate into the military stores and sealed the depot with Wei.

sentences.zh: 均眾皆銀槍繡衣，為數隊，分列子城中。

translations.literal: Jun's host all had silver spears and embroidered robes, formed into several companies, and were arrayed separately in the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's troops, armed with silver spears and in embroidered robes, formed several companies posted throughout the inner city.

sentences.zh: 賊兵出通遠門，與懷忠戰數合，會暮，懷忠復退軍筰橋，背水列陣，砦櫧木橋南，以扞邛、蜀之路。

translations.literal: Bandit troops issued from Tongyuan Gate and fought several rounds with Huaizhong; at dusk Huaizhong again withdrew his army to Zhua Bridge, drew up in formation with water at his back, and encamped south of Zhumu Bridge to block the roads to Qiong and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels came out Tongyuan Gate and clashed with Huaizhong several times; at dusk he withdrew to Zhua Bridge, formed up with his back to the water, and camped south of Zhumu Bridge to hold the Qiong and Shu roads.

sentences.zh: 賊故不復能南略，自清水壩、溫江、金馬三道來攻櫧木砦，出官軍後，焚江原神祠，斷邛、蜀援路。

translations.literal: The bandits therefore could no longer advance south; from the three routes of Qingshui Dam, Wenjiang, and Jinma they came to attack Zhumu Fort, emerged behind the imperial army, burned the Jiangyuan spirit shrine, and cut the relief routes to Qiong and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked from advancing south, the rebels attacked Zhumu Fort by three routes—Qingshui Dam, Wenjiang, and Jinma—got behind the imperial army, burned the Jiangyuan shrine, and severed relief routes to Qiong and Shu.

sentences.zh: 懷忠三路分兵以抗之，斬首五百餘級，驅其餘眾入皂江，獲甲弩甚眾。

translations.literal: Huaizhong divided his troops along three routes to resist them, beheaded more than five hundred, drove the rest into Zao River, and captured very many armor and crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhong split his forces three ways, killed more than five hundred, drove the rest into the Zao River, and seized a great quantity of armor and crossbows.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐賊至益州南十五里，砦於雞鳴原，以俟王師。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory, he pursued the bandits to fifteen li south of Yizhou, encamped at Jiming Plain, and waited for the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fleeing rebels fifteen li south of Yizhou, encamped at Jiming Plain, and awaited the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 均亦閉成都東門以自固。

translations.literal: Jun also closed the east gate of Chengdu to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jun likewise shut Chengdu's east gate to fortify his position.

sentences.zh: 是月，有終等至，令石普先與綿漢都巡檢張思鈞收復漢州，進壁升僊橋。

translations.literal: That month Youzhong and the others arrived; he ordered Shi Pu first, together with Mian-Han Metropolitan Inspector Zhang Sijun, to recover Hanzhou and advance to encamp at Shengxian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: That month Youzhong arrived and sent Shi Pu with Mian-Han Metropolitan Inspector Zhang Sijun to retake Hanzhou and encamp at Shengxian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 賊出攻砦，有終擊走之。

translations.literal: Bandits came out to attack the fort; Youzhong struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked the camp, Youzhong drove them off.

sentences.zh: 一日，均開城偽為遁狀，有終與上官正、石普率兵徑入，官軍分剽民財，部伍不肅。

translations.literal: One day Jun opened the city feigning flight; Youzhong, Shangguan Zheng, and Shi Pu led troops straight in; the imperial army dispersed to plunder the people's property, and ranks were not disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: One day Jun opened the gates as if to flee; Youzhong, Shangguan Zheng, and Shi Pu marched straight in, but the troops scattered to loot civilians and discipline collapsed.

sentences.zh: 賊閉關發伏，布床榻於路口，官軍不得出，因為所殺。

translations.literal: The bandits closed the passes and sprung ambushes, laid beds and couches at the crossroads, and the imperial army could not get out—thus they were slain.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shut the gates, sprung ambushes, and blocked the exits with bedding; trapped, the imperial troops were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 有終等緣堞而墜，李惠死之，退保漢州。

translations.literal: Youzhong and the others climbed down along the battlements; Li Hui died in the action, and they withdrew to hold Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong and others escaped over the battlements; Li Hui was killed, and they fell back to Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 益州城中民皆奔迸四出，復為賊黨分騎追殺，或囚縶之，支解族誅以恐眾。

translations.literal: The people of Yizhou city all fled bursting out in every direction; again rebel partisans divided cavalry to pursue and kill them, or imprisoned them, dismembering them and executing whole clans to terrify the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou's people fled in all directions; rebel horsemen hunted them down, imprisoned others, and dismembered them or executed whole families to terrify the populace.

sentences.zh: 又脅士民僧道之少壯者為兵，先刺手背，次髡首，次黥面，給軍裝，令乘城，與舊賊黨相間。

translations.literal: They also coerced young and strong among gentlemen, commoners, monks, and Taoists to serve as soldiers: first tattoo the back of the hand, next shave the head, next brand the face, issue military gear, order them to man the walls, interspersed with old bandit partisans.
translations.idiomatic: They also pressed young gentry, commoners, monks, and priests into service—first tattooing their hands, then shaving their heads, then branding their faces—issued them arms, and posted them on the walls alongside veteran rebels.

sentences.zh: 有終署榜招之，至則署其衣袂釋之，日數百人。

translations.literal: Youzhong posted placards to summon them; when they came he marked their sleeves and released them—several hundred a day.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong posted notices summoning them; those who came had their sleeves marked and were released—several hundred each day.

sentences.zh: 三月，進攻彌牟砦，斬首千餘級，復為賊所拒。

translations.literal: In the third month, advancing to attack Mimu Fort, they beheaded more than a thousand, but again were repelled by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month they attacked Mimu Fort, killed more than a thousand, but were repelled again.

sentences.zh: 四月，賊由升僊橋分路來寇，並軍於東偏，有終率兵逆擊，大敗之，殺千餘人，奪其傘蓋、金槍等物，均單騎還城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, bandits came to raid by separate routes from Shengxian Bridge and united their armies on the eastern flank; Youzhong led troops to meet and strike, routed them utterly, killed more than a thousand, seized their parasols, canopies, gold spears, and the like; Jun returned to the city alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month rebels advanced by several routes from Shengxian Bridge and massed on the east; Youzhong counterattacked, routed them, killed more than a thousand, and seized their banners, parasols, and gold spears; Jun fled back to the city alone.

sentences.zh: 有終遣其子奉禮郎孝若馳奏，上召孝若問敗賊之由，笑謂左右曰：「均鼠竊爾，雖嬰城自守，計日可擒矣。」

translations.literal: Youzhong dispatched his son Palace Attendant-in-Waiting Xiaoruo by rapid memorial; the emperor summoned Xiaoruo and asked the reason for defeating the bandits, and smiling said to those beside him: "Jun is a mere rodent thief; though he clings to the city in defense, within days he can be captured."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong sent his son Xiaoruo with a memorial by relay; the emperor summoned him and asked how the rebels had been beaten, then smiled and told his attendants, "Jun is nothing but a rat thief; even walled up in the city, he can be taken within days."

sentences.zh: 孝若因言嘗習武藝，願改秩以效，即補供奉官。

translations.literal: Xiaoruo then said he had practiced martial arts and wished to change rank to serve; he was immediately appointed Attendant Official.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoruo said he had trained in martial arts and wished to serve in a military post; he was immediately made an attendant official.

sentences.zh: 俄以刑部員外郎馬亮為轉運使，國子博士張志言副之，供備庫副使張晌為綿漢都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Shortly Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Ma Liang was made transport commissioner, National University Academician Zhang Zhiyan was made his deputy, and Deputy Commissioner of the Supply Repository Zhang Shang was made Mian-Han Metropolitan Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ma Liang was made transport commissioner with National University Academician Zhang Zhiyan as his deputy, and Supply Repository Deputy Commissioner Zhang Shang was made Mian-Han metropolitan inspector.

sentences.zh: 楊懷忠又分所部砦於合水尾、浣花等處，樹機石、設笓籬以拒之。

translations.literal: Yang Huaizhong again divided his command to encamp at Heshuiwei, Huanhua, and other places, erected rolling logs and set palisades to resist them.
