translations.idiomatic: Yang Huaizhong posted detachments at Heshuiwei, Huanhua, and elsewhere, setting up rolling logs and palisades to block the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊自升僊之敗，徹橋塞門，官軍進至清還江，為梁而度。

translations.literal: After their defeat at Shengxian, the bandits dismantled bridges and blocked gates; the imperial army advanced to Qinghuan River, built a bridge, and crossed.
translations.idiomatic: After their defeat at Shengxian Bridge, the rebels destroyed bridges and sealed the gates; the imperial army reached Qinghuan River, built a bridge, and crossed.

sentences.zh: 有終與石普屯於城北門之西，依壕為土山，分設鹿角，又得舊草場，造梯衝洞車攻具，普專主之。

translations.literal: Youzhong and Shi Pu encamped west of the north city gate, piled earthen mounds along the moat, distributed abatis, and also recovered an old meadow to build scaling ladders, battering rams, covered approaches, and other siege equipment—Pu was put solely in charge of this.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong and Shi Pu camped west of the north gate, piled earthworks along the moat, laid abatis, and on an old parade ground built scaling ladders, battering rams, and covered approaches; Shi Pu directed the siege works.

sentences.zh: 高繼勳、張晌、孫正辭攻城東，上官正、李繼昌、王阮攻城西，楊懷忠與巡檢殿直、閤門祗候馬貴攻城南，賊將趙延順盡驅凶黨以拒。

translations.literal: Gao Jixun, Zhang Shang, and Sun Zhengci attacked the east of the city; Shangguan Zheng, Li Jichang, and Wang Ruan attacked the west; Yang Huaizhong, together with Inspection Captain and Gate Aide Ma Gui, attacked the south; the bandit general Zhao Yanshun drove all ferocious partisans to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jixun, Zhang Shang, and Sun Zhengci assaulted the east; Shangguan Zheng, Li Jichang, and Wang Ruan the west; Yang Huaizhong and Gate Aide Ma Gui the south; rebel general Zhao Yanshun threw every hardened follower into the defense.

sentences.zh: 既而延順中流矢死，又遣其黨丁重萬立城門上，官軍射之，殪。

translations.literal: Before long Yanshun was struck by a flying arrow and died; they again sent his partisan Ding Chongwan to stand atop the city gate; the imperial army shot him, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshun was soon killed by an arrow; the rebels then posted his follower Ding Chongwan on the gate tower, and imperial archers shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 每攻城，輒會雨，城滑不能上，官軍及丁夫為洞屋以進，賊又鑿地道出掩之，溺壕中死者千餘，軍勢小衄。

translations.literal: Each time they assaulted the city, rain would coincide; the walls were slippery and could not be scaled; the imperial army and corvée laborers advanced in covered approaches, but the bandits also dug tunnels to emerge and strike them from behind; more than a thousand drowned in the moat and died—the army's momentum suffered a small setback.
translations.idiomatic: Each assault coincided with rain; the walls were too slick to climb, so troops and laborers advanced under covered approaches, but rebels tunneled out to ambush them; more than a thousand drowned in the moat, and momentum faltered.

sentences.zh: 時方暑濕，軍士多疾，有終市藥他州療之。

translations.literal: At this time it was hot and humid; many soldiers fell ill; Youzhong purchased medicine from other prefectures to treat them.
translations.idiomatic: In the humid heat many troops fell ill; Youzhong bought medicine from neighboring prefectures to treat them.

sentences.zh: 是月，詔洛苑使、入內副都知秦翰為兩川捉賊招安使。

translations.literal: That month an edict made Luoyuan Commissioner and Inner Palace Deputy Chief Controller Qin Han pacification-and-capture commissioner for the Two Circuits of Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: That month Qin Han, Luoyuan commissioner and inner-palace deputy chief, was made pacification commissioner for the Two Chuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 有終與翰叶議，於城北魚橋又築土山。

translations.literal: Youzhong and Han deliberated together and at Yujiao north of the city again built earthen mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong and Qin Han agreed to raise another earthwork north of the city at Yujiao Bridge.

sentences.zh: 八月，克城北羊馬城，遂設雁翅敵棚，覆洞屋以進，逼羅城。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they took the sheep-and-horse wall north of the city, then set up goose-wing enemy sheds, advanced under covered approaches, and pressed close to the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they took the northern sheep-and-horse wall, erected angled enemy sheds, advanced under covered approaches, and closed on the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 九月，城北洞屋成，賊對設敵樓以抗官軍，有終遣卒焚之，賊自是銷沮，築月城以自固。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the covered approaches north of the city were completed; the bandits set up facing enemy towers to resist the imperial army; Youzhong sent soldiers to burn them; from this the bandits grew discouraged and built a crescent wall to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the northern covered approaches were finished; rebels raised opposing towers, but Youzhong sent men to burn them; their morale collapsed, and they built a crescent rampart for defense.

sentences.zh: 有終募敢死士間道以入，賊為藥矢，中者立死。

translations.literal: Youzhong recruited dare-to-die soldiers to enter by hidden paths; the bandits made poisoned arrows—those struck died at once.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong recruited volunteers to infiltrate by hidden routes; the rebels used poisoned arrows that killed on contact.

sentences.zh: 有終令卒蒙氈秉燧以入，悉焚其望櫓機石，先遣東西南砦鼓噪攻城，有終與石普分主洞屋以進。

translations.literal: Youzhong ordered soldiers to enter draped in felt, carrying torches, and burned all their watch towers and rolling logs; first he sent the eastern, southern, and western forts to beat drums and shout in assault on the city; Youzhong and Shi Pu each commanded covered approaches to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong had troops enter under felt blankets with torches and burn the watchtowers and rolling logs; he first sent eastern, southern, and western camps to storm the walls with drum and shout while he and Shi Pu led covered approaches forward separately.

sentences.zh: 普穴城為暗門，門成，賊攢戟於前，無敢進者。

translations.literal: Pu tunneled into the wall for a hidden gate; when the gate was completed, the bandits massed halberds before it and none dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu tunneled a secret gate through the wall; when it opened, rebels massed halberds at the breach and no one dared enter.

sentences.zh: 有二卒請行，許以厚賞，乃麾戈直衝之，賊鋒稍卻，遂入城。

translations.literal: Two soldiers requested to go; promised rich reward, they then waved spears and charged straight in; the bandit vanguard withdrew somewhat, and they entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Two soldiers volunteered, were promised rich reward, charged straight in with spears, forced the rebel line back, and broke into the city.

sentences.zh: 有終登城樓下瞰，賊之餘眾，猶砦天長觀前，於文翁坊密設炮架。

translations.literal: Youzhong ascended a city tower and looked down: the bandits' remaining host still encamped before Tiangchang Temple and secretly set up catapult frames at Wengong Lane.
translations.idiomatic: From a tower Youzhong looked down on the rebels' remaining force still camped before Tiangchang Temple, with catapults secretly positioned at Wengong Lane.

sentences.zh: 高繼勳白於馬亮，請給稭稈油籸，眾執長戟巨斧，秉炬以進，悉焚之。

translations.literal: Gao Jixun reported to Ma Liang, requesting straw, oil, and chaff; the host grasped long halberds and great axes, bearing torches as they advanced, and burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jixun asked Ma Liang for straw, oil, and chaff; troops advanced with long halberds, great axes, and torches and burned the positions entirely.

sentences.zh: 楊懷忠焚其砦天長觀前，追至大安門，復敗焉。

translations.literal: Yang Huaizhong burned their fort before Tiangchang Temple, pursued to Da'an Gate, and again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huaizhong burned the camp before Tiangchang Temple, pursued to Da'an Gate, and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 是夕二鼓，均與其黨二萬餘南出萬里橋門，突圍而遁。

translations.literal: That evening at the second watch, Jun and his partisans, more than twenty thousand, went south out Wanli Bridge Gate, broke the encirclement, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the second watch Jun and more than twenty thousand followers broke out south through Wanli Bridge Gate and fled.

sentences.zh: 有終疑有伏，遣人縱火城中。

translations.literal: Youzhong suspected an ambush and sent men to set fires throughout the city.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting an ambush, Youzhong had the city set afire.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，與秦翰登門樓，牙吏有受偽署官職者，捕得，立樓下，傍積薪，厝火其上，索男子魁壯者令辨之，曰某嘗受某職，即命左右捽投火中。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, together with Qin Han he ascended the gate tower; a clerk who had received a spurious appointment to office was captured, made to stand below the tower with firewood piled beside him and fire set atop it; strong adult males were sought to identify them—if one said so-and-so had once received such-and-such a post, he immediately ordered attendants to seize and throw him into the fire.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he and Qin Han mounted the gate tower; a clerk who had taken a rebel appointment was captured and bound below a pile of kindling; stout men were brought to identify collaborators—if anyone named a man and his rebel title, attendants seized him and threw him into the fire.

sentences.zh: 自晨至晡，焚死者數百人，時謂冤酷。

translations.literal: From morning to late afternoon, several hundred were burned to death; contemporaries called it cruel injustice.
translations.idiomatic: From morning till afternoon several hundred were burned alive—an act contemporaries denounced as cruel injustice.

sentences.zh: 均既走，度合水尾，由廣都略陵、榮，趣富順監，所過斷橋塞路，焚倉庫而去。

translations.literal: After Jun had fled, he crossed Heshuiwei, passed through Guangdu toward Ling and Rong, and hastened to Fushun Superintendency; wherever he passed he destroyed bridges, blocked roads, burned storehouses, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun fled across Heshuiwei, crossed Guangdu toward Ling and Rong, and made for Fushun Superintendency, destroying bridges, blocking roads, and burning storehouses as he went.

sentences.zh: 初，有終遣懷忠領虎翼軍追之，後二日，石普繼往，以全軍為後援。

translations.literal: At first Youzhong dispatched Huaizhong to lead the Tiger-Wing Army in pursuit; two days later Shi Pu followed, with the full army as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong first sent Huaizhong with the Tiger-Wing Army in pursuit; two days later Shi Pu followed with the main army as reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 十月，均至富順，其將校以筏度江，趨戎、瀘蠻境。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Jun reached Fushun; his officers and commanders crossed the river on rafts and hastened toward the Yi and Lu barbarian frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Jun reached Fushun; his officers crossed the river on rafts and headed for the Yi and Lu tribal frontier.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每歲孟冬朔，詔富順監具酒肴，犒內屬蠻酋。

translations.literal: Every year on the first day of the first month of winter, the court issued an edict for Fushun Superintendency to prepare wine and viands to reward affiliated barbarian chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on the first day of winter the court ordered Fushun Superintendency to prepare wine and food to reward affiliated tribal chiefs.

sentences.zh: 是日裁設具，而均黨適至，皆食焉。

translations.literal: That day the provisions had just been set out when Jun's partisans happened to arrive—and all ate of them.
translations.idiomatic: That day the feast had just been laid when Jun's followers arrived and ate it all.

sentences.zh: 聞懷忠追騎將至，均心易之，謂其黨曰：「速降懷忠。」

translations.literal: Hearing that Huaizhong's pursuing cavalry were about to arrive, Jun took it lightly and said to his partisans: "Quickly surrender to Huaizhong."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Huaizhong's cavalry were near, Jun grew overconfident and told his men, "Surrender to Huaizhong at once."

sentences.zh: 令其眾負擔以行。

translations.literal: He ordered his host to carry burdens as they marched.
translations.idiomatic: He had his men pack up and march.

sentences.zh: 懷忠距富順六十里，於楊家市少憩，賊眾在後者邀戰，懷忠遣騎士登高原覘賊，且語其左右曰：「縱賊度江，後悔無及，聞石侯將至，當以奇兵取之。」

translations.literal: Huaizhong was sixty li from Fushun and rested briefly at Yangjia Market; bandits among those in the rear challenged to battle; Huaizhong sent horsemen to ascend the high plain to reconnoiter the bandits, and also said to those beside him: "If we let the bandits cross the river, regret will come too late; I hear Lord Shi is about to arrive—we should take them with unexpected troops."
translations.idiomatic: Sixty li from Fushun, Huaizhong paused at Yangjia Market; straggling rebels behind him offered battle; he sent horsemen to a height to scout them and told his officers, "If they cross the river we shall regret it; Shi Pu is coming—we should take them by surprise."

sentences.zh: 乃臨江列陣擊之，餘黨散走，有舟將度江而遁者，懷忠合強弩射之，溺死甚眾。

translations.literal: He then drew up in formation along the river and struck them; the remaining partisans scattered and fled; those with boats about to cross the river and escape—Huaizhong gathered strong crossbows to shoot them, and very many drowned and died.
translations.idiomatic: He formed up along the river and attacked; scattered rebels fled, but those trying to cross by boat were cut down by crossbow fire and drowned in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 懷忠張旗鳴鼙入城，均方在監署中，其眾多醉，均窮蹙縊死。

translations.literal: Huaizhong raised banners and beat war drums entering the city; Jun was just then in the superintendency office; his host was mostly drunk; Jun, in desperate straits, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhong entered the city with banners raised and drums beating; Jun was in the superintendency office, his men mostly drunk; cornered, Jun hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 虎翼軍校魯斌斬其首詣懷忠，獲僭偽法物、旌旗、甲馬甚眾，禽其黨六千餘人，逆徒殲焉。

translations.literal: Tiger-Wing Army captain Lu Bin cut off his head and presented it to Huaizhong; very many usurped regalia, banners, flags, armor, and horses were captured; more than six thousand of his partisans were taken—the rebels were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger-Wing captain Lu Bin brought Jun's head to Huaizhong; they seized rebel regalia, banners, armor, and horses in quantity and captured more than six thousand followers—the rebellion was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 懷忠旋軍出北門，石普之眾方至，奪均首馳歸成都，梟於北市。

translations.literal: Huaizhong turned his army and exited the north gate; Shi Pu's host had just arrived; he seized Jun's head and galloped back to Chengdu, where it was displayed in the north market.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhong marched out the north gate as Shi Pu's force arrived; Shi Pu took Jun's head, raced back to Chengdu, and displayed it in the north market.

sentences.zh: 均本隸開封散從直，後補軍校。

translations.literal: Jun had originally served among the Kaifeng miscellaneous attendants, and was later appointed army captain.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had originally served among Kaifeng's miscellaneous attendants and was later made an army captain.

sentences.zh: 初，神衛軍之戍成都者，以均及董福分二指揮以領之。

translations.literal: At first the Divine Guards garrisoned at Chengdu had Jun and Dong Fu divide two commands to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengdu garrison of the Divine Guards had been divided into two commands under Jun and Dong Fu.

sentences.zh: 福御眾有法，部下皆優足。

translations.literal: Fu governed the host with method; his subordinates were all well provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Fu kept strict discipline; his men were well supplied.

sentences.zh: 均縱其下飲博，軍裝亦以給費。

translations.literal: Jun indulged his subordinates in drinking and gambling, and military gear was also spent on expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Jun let his men drink and gamble freely, and even army gear was squandered on their expenses.

sentences.zh: 是歲，車駕幸河朔，符昭壽與牛冕大閱於東郊，蜀人趨觀之，二軍衣服鮮弊不等，均眾因是慚憤。

translations.literal: That year the imperial carriage visited Heshuo; Fu Zhaoshou and Niu Mian reviewed troops in great ceremony at the eastern suburb; Shu people rushed to watch; the clothing of the two armies—fresh and worn—was unequal; Jun's host therefore felt ashamed and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: That year, while the emperor toured Heshuo, Fu Zhaoshou and Niu Mian held a grand review in the eastern suburbs; Shu onlookers saw Jun's troops in shabbier dress than Dong Fu's, and humiliation bred resentment.

sentences.zh: 益州知州與鈐轄二廨並禁旅為牙隊，歲除，冕以酒肴犒部士，而昭壽既驕恣，復肆侵虐，冕亦寬馳無政，故詰朝合起為亂。

translations.literal: The Yizhou prefect and the two offices of military controller and the prohibited brigade served together as the guard company; at year's end Mian rewarded departmental soldiers with wine and viands, but Zhaoshou was both arrogant and willful and again wantonly encroached and abused; Mian also was lax and without governance—hence the next morning together they rose in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: The Yizhou prefect and military controllers shared garrison duty as one guard company; at New Year's Eve Niu Mian feasted his men, but Fu Zhaoshou was arrogant and abusive while Mian was lax—so on New Year's morning the garrison mutinied together.

sentences.zh: 神衛卒既殺昭壽，是日，成都官吏方相與賀正，聞變，皆奔竄，牛冕與轉運張適縋城而出，惟都巡檢使劉紹榮冒刃格鬥。

translations.literal: Once the Divine Guard soldiers had killed Zhaoshou, that day Chengdu officials were just congratulating one another on the New Year; hearing the upheaval, all fled in panic; Niu Mian and Transport Commissioner Zhang Shi lowered themselves by rope over the wall and escaped; only Metropolitan Inspector Liu Shaorong braved blades in hand-to-hand combat.
translations.idiomatic: After the Divine Guards killed Fu Zhaoshou, Chengdu officials were exchanging New Year's greetings when word of the mutiny sent them fleeing; Niu Mian and Transport Commissioner Zhang Shi escaped over the wall by rope; only Metropolitan Inspector Liu Shaorong fought on through the blades.

sentences.zh: 既而眾寡不敵，叛卒尚未有主，或欲奉紹榮為帥者，紹榮攝弓罵曰：「我燕人也，比棄鄉土來歸本朝，豈能與汝同逆，汝亟殺我，我肯負朝廷哉！」

translations.literal: Before long, few against many, they could not match them; the rebel soldiers still had no leader; some wished to install Shaorong as commander; Shaorong nocked his bow and cursed, saying: "I am a man of Yan; I abandoned my native land to come and submit to this dynasty—how can I join you in rebellion? Quickly kill me—I would never betray the court!"
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, the mutineers still lacked a leader; some wanted Liu Shaorong as commander; he strung his bow and shouted, "I am a man of Yan who left my homeland to serve this dynasty—how can I join your revolt? Kill me if you will—I will never betray the court!"

sentences.zh: 眾未敢動。

translations.literal: The host did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers did not dare touch him.

sentences.zh: 監軍王澤與均適至，乃謂均曰：「汝所部為亂，盍自往招安？」

translations.literal: Army Supervisor Wang Ze and Jun happened to arrive; he then said to Jun: "Your command has risen in revolt—why not go yourself to pacify them?"
translations.idiomatic: Army Supervisor Wang Ze arrived with Jun and said, "Your men have mutinied—why not go pacify them yourself?"

sentences.zh: 均既往，叛卒即擁之為主，紹榮自經死。

translations.literal: When Jun went, the rebel soldiers immediately installed him as leader; Shaorong hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jun went; the mutineers immediately made him their leader; Liu Shaorong hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 均僭號大蜀，改元化順，署置官稱，設貢舉，以張鍇為謀主。

translations.literal: Jun presumptuously styled himself Great Shu, changed the era name to Huashun, appointed official titles, established the civil examinations, and made Zhang Kai his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Jun proclaimed himself ruler of Great Shu, adopted the era name Huashun, set up a court and civil examinations, and made Zhang Kai his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 鍇本名美，太原舊卒，後為神衛小校。

translations.literal: Kai's original name was Mei; he was an old soldier of Taiyuan and later became a minor captain of the Divine Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai, originally named Mei, was a veteran from Taiyuan who later became a minor Divine Guards captain.

sentences.zh: 狡獪，嘗歷戰陣，粗習陰陽，以熒惑同惡，故勸均為亂。

translations.literal: He was cunning and slippery, had once passed through battle lines, had rough knowledge of yin and yang, and by dazzling and bewitching shared their evil—hence he urged Jun to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Cunning and battle-tested, with a rough knowledge of astrology, he swayed like-minded men and urged Jun to rebel.

sentences.zh: 均實戇愞無謀，嘗言：「官軍若至，我當先路出迎，自陳被脅之狀。」

translations.literal: Jun was in truth dull and stubborn without stratagem; he once said: "If the imperial army arrives, I shall go out first on the road to welcome them and explain myself as having been coerced."
translations.idiomatic: Jun was slow-witted and without strategy; he once said, "When the imperial army comes, I shall go out to meet them first and explain that I was forced into this."

sentences.zh: 鍇聞之，擇軍中子弟署寄班，以防守均，令不與人接見。

translations.literal: When Kai heard this, he chose young men among the army and appointed them as palace attendants to guard Jun, ordering that he receive no visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Zhang Kai picked young soldiers as palace attendants to guard Jun and barred all visitors.

sentences.zh: 官軍圍城，每射箭招誘，及令均子弟至城下，均皆不之知。

translations.literal: When the imperial army besieged the city, each time they shot in arrows to entice and summon, and even when they had Jun's own kinsmen come below the wall, Jun knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege the imperial army sent in arrows summoning surrender and even brought Jun's relatives to the wall, but he knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 得箭書，鍇悉焚之。

translations.literal: Whenever arrow letters were received, Kai burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai burned every message sent in on arrows.

sentences.zh: 自起至敗，所守止一城而已。

translations.literal: From rising to defeat, what he held was only one city.
translations.idiomatic: From outbreak to defeat he held only a single city.

sentences.zh: 均初署親軍為天降虎翼，後果為虎翼軍所殺。

translations.literal: Jun at first styled his personal army the Heaven-descended Tiger-Wing; in the end he was indeed killed by the Tiger-Wing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had named his personal guard the Heaven-sent Tiger-Wing Army—and was indeed killed by the Tiger-Wing Army.

sentences.zh: 賊既平，遣承受供奉官楊崇勳乘傳告捷，賜崇勳錦袍、銀帶、器幣，有終加保信軍節度觀察留後，以秦翰為內園使、恩州刺史，石普為冀州團練使，高繼勳、王阮並為崇儀使，孫正辭為內殿崇班，李繼昌為獎州刺史，張晌為供備庫副使，楊懷忠為供備庫副使，馬貴為供奉官。

translations.literal: Once the bandits were pacified, Attendant Official Yang Chongxun was dispatched by post relay to report victory; Chongxun was granted brocade robes, a silver belt, and ceremonial vessels; Youzhong was promoted to Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Baoxin Army as acting regent; Qin Han was made Inner Garden Commissioner and prefect of Enzhou; Shi Pu was made regimental commissioner of Jizhou; Gao Jixun and Wang Ruan were both made Honored Ceremonial Commissioners; Sun Zhengci was made Inner Hall Honored Company; Li Jichang was made prefect of Jiangzhou; Zhang Shang was made Deputy Commissioner of the Supply Repository; Yang Huaizhong was made Deputy Commissioner of the Supply Repository; Ma Gui was made Attendant Official.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, Attendant Official Yang Chongxun was sent to report victory; he received brocade robes, a silver belt, and gifts; Youzhong was made acting military governor of Baoxin Army; Qin Han was made inner-garden commissioner and prefect of Enzhou; Shi Pu regimental commissioner of Jizhou; Gao Jixun and Wang Ruan honored ceremonial commissioners; Sun Zhengci inner-hall honored company; Li Jichang prefect of Jiangzhou; Zhang Shang and Yang Huaizhong deputy supply commissioners; Ma Gui an attendant official.

sentences.zh: 是役也，懷忠之功居最，為石普所忌，朝廷微聞之，遣寄班安守忠按視戰所，盡得其功狀，以故懷忠復遷崇儀使，領恩州刺史。

translations.literal: In this campaign Huaizhong's merit ranked first; he was envied by Shi Pu; the court faintly heard of it and dispatched Palace Attendant An Shouzhong to inspect the battle site and fully obtain records of his achievements—for this reason Huaizhong was again promoted Honored Ceremonial Commissioner, concurrently governing Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign Huaizhong's service ranked first, arousing Shi Pu's jealousy; the court heard faint rumors and sent Palace Attendant An Shouzhong to review the battlefield and document his deeds; Huaizhong was therefore promoted to honored ceremonial commissioner and made prefect of Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，有終代還，命為涇、原、儀、渭、鎮戎路都部署，辭不拜，改知永興軍府，徙秦州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Youzhong returned on replacement; he was appointed Overall Commander of the Jing, Yuan, Yi, Wei, and Zhenrong Route; he declined to accept and was changed to govern Yongxing Military Prefecture, then transferred to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Youzhong returned from Sichuan; offered overall command of the Jing-Yuan-Yi-Wei-Zhenrong circuit, he declined and was made prefect of Yongxing, then transferred to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，徙為幷代副都部署，賜黃金四百兩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was transferred to Deputy Overall Commander of Bing and Dai and granted four hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era he was made deputy overall commander of Bing and Dai and awarded four hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，起復，契丹入寇，上幸澶淵，詔有終率所部由土門抵鎮州，與大兵會。

translations.literal: Mourning his mother, he was recalled to office before mourning ended; the Khitan invaded; the emperor visited Chanyuan; an edict ordered Youzhong to lead his command by Tumen to reach Zhenzhou and join the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Called back from mourning for his mother, he was ordered when the Khitan invaded and the emperor marched to Chanyuan to lead his troops through Tumen Pass to Zhenzhou to join the main army.

sentences.zh: 既而王超、桑贊逗撓無功，唯有終赴援，威聲甚振，河北列城，賴其雄張。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Chao and Sang Zan stalled and achieved nothing; only Youzhong went to the rescue; his martial renown shook greatly; the walled cities of Hebei relied on his powerful presence.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Chao and Sang Zan dithered without result, only Youzhong marched to the rescue; his reputation shook the north, and Hebei's garrison cities rested on his strength.

sentences.zh: 俄而契丹修好，命還屯所，就判并州，召拜宣徽北院使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: Shortly the Khitan made peace; he was ordered to return and garrison his post, concurrently judging Bingzhou, and summoned and appointed North Privy Council Commissioner and Grand Mentor with the checking-only title.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was made with the Khitan he returned to his post, was made concurrent governor of Bingzhou, and was summoned as North Privy Council commissioner and Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，暴疾卒，年五十九，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year he died suddenly of illness, aged fifty-nine; he was posthumously granted Chamberlain for Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year he died suddenly at fifty-nine and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 錄其子孝若為內殿崇班、閤門祗候，孝傑為內殿崇班，孝緒為供奉官，孝恭為侍禁，親族、門客、給事輩遷補者八人。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoruo was entered in the rolls as Inner Hall Honored Company and Gate Aide; Xiaojie as Inner Hall Honored Company; Xiaoxu as Attendant Official; Xiaogong as Palace Guard; eight among kinsmen, retainers, and household attendants were transferred and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xiaoruo, Xiaojie, Xiaoxu, and Xiaogong were given court posts, and eight kinsmen, retainers, and household staff were also promoted.

sentences.zh: 有終倜儻自任，不拘小節，有幹局，沈敏善斷，不畏強禦，輕財好施。

translations.literal: Youzhong was free-spirited and self-reliant, unconstrained by petty details; he had administrative capacity, was deep and keen and good at deciding, feared no powerful adversary, and was light with wealth and fond of giving.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong was bold and independent, careless of small proprieties yet capable in affairs—shrewd, decisive, unafraid of the powerful, generous with his money.

sentences.zh: 歷典藩閫，能撫士卒，豐於宴犒，官用不足，則傾私帑及榷錢以給之。

translations.literal: Through successive governorships of frontier commands he could soothe soldiers, was lavish in feasts and rewards; when official funds were insufficient, he emptied private coffers and monopoly revenues to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: As a frontier commander he won over his troops with lavish feasts; when official funds ran short he drew on his private purse and monopoly revenues to pay them.

sentences.zh: 家無餘財，奉身甚薄，常所御者，銅鞍勒馬而已。

translations.literal: His household had no surplus wealth; he maintained himself very sparely; what he regularly used was only a copper saddle and bridle on his horse.
translations.idiomatic: He left no fortune at home, lived plainly himself, and rode only a horse with a copper saddle and bridle.

sentences.zh: 第在崇仁里者，德驤所創。

translations.literal: The mansion in Chongren Lane was founded by Dexiang.
translations.idiomatic: The mansion in Chongren Lane had been built by his father Dexiang.

sentences.zh: 有終在蜀嘗貸備用庫錢數百萬，奏納其第償之，優詔蠲免。

translations.literal: While in Shu Youzhong once borrowed several million in cash from the standby treasury; he memorialized offering his mansion to repay it—a gracious edict remitted the debt.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu he had borrowed millions from the standby treasury and offered his mansion in repayment; the emperor graciously remitted the debt.

sentences.zh: 為宣徽使，特給廉鎮公用錢歲二千貫。

translations.literal: As Privy Council Commissioner he was specially granted two thousand strings of public funds for his clean command each year.
translations.idiomatic: As privy council commissioner he received two thousand strings annually for official entertainments.

sentences.zh: 身沒之日，宿負猶不啻千萬，官為償之。

translations.literal: On the day his body perished, outstanding debts still amounted to no less than ten million; the state repaid them.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he still owed more than ten million; the state paid his debts.

sentences.zh: 王繼英在樞密，頗忌有終進用，屢言其在蜀及守邊厚費以收士卒心，真宗不之信，卒保護焉。

translations.literal: Wang Jiying was in the Privy Council and rather envied Youzhong's advancement; he repeatedly spoke of his heavy spending in Shu and on guarding the frontier to win soldiers' hearts; Zhenzong did not believe it and ultimately protected him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiying at the Privy Council envied Youzhong's rise and repeatedly accused him of buying troop loyalty with lavish spending in Shu and on the frontier; Zhenzong disbelieved him and continued to protect Youzhong.

sentences.zh: 孫 孝先

translations.literal: Grandson: Xiaoxian
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Sun Xiaoxian

sentences.zh: 孝先，字子思，有鄰子也。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian, style name Zisi, was a son of Youlin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxian, courtesy name Zisi, was a son of Lei Youlin.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，試秘書省校書郎，知天長縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was tested as proofreader of the Secretariat, and served as magistrate of Tianchang County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat, and served as magistrate of Tianchang County.

sentences.zh: 以衛濯訟其內亂，除籍配均州。

translations.literal: Because Wei Zhuo sued him for domestic disorder, his name was struck from the rolls and he was assigned to Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhuo sued him for incest; his name was struck from the rolls and he was exiled to Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 後復知宛丘縣，李繼隆判陳州，薦其能，加試大理評事。

translations.literal: Later he again served as magistrate of Wanqiu County; Li Jilong, as military commissioner of Chenzhou, recommended his ability, and he was additionally tested as judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again appointed magistrate of Wanqiu. Li Jilong, serving as military commissioner of Chenzhou, recommended his talent, and Sun Xiaoxian was given an additional appointment as judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 契丹內寇，真宗幸大名，孝先以部芻糧河北，首至行在，擢太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided within the borders, Emperor Zhenzong traveled to Daming; Xiaoxian led forage from Hebei and was first to reach the imperial camp, and was promoted to Ceremonial Usher of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded, Emperor Zhenzong went to Daming. Sun Xiaoxian led forage supplies from Hebei and was the first to reach the imperial camp, whereupon he was promoted to Ceremonial Usher in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 王均反益州，隨季父有終進討，孝先率先鋒與賊戰升僊橋，斬首數百，得均金槍黃傘以獻，改將作監丞。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun rebelled in Yizhou, he followed his uncle Youzhong on the punitive campaign; Xiaoxian led the vanguard and fought the rebels at Shengxian Bridge, beheading several hundred; he seized Wang Jun's golden spear and yellow parasol and presented them, and was changed to Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun rebelled in Yizhou, Sun Xiaoxian followed his uncle Lei Youzhong on the punitive campaign. He led the vanguard against the rebels at Shengxian Bridge, took several hundred heads, seized Wang Jun's golden spear and yellow parasol as trophies, and was appointed Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷陷靈州，朝廷調兵，軍費多出於民，關內大擾。

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian seized Lingzhou, the court mobilized troops; military expenses largely came from the people, and Guanzhong was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Jiqian seized Lingzhou, the court mobilized troops; military costs fell heavily on the people, and Guanzhong was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 孝先請益募商人入粟塞下，償以茶鹽。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian requested additionally recruiting merchants to bring grain below the passes, repaying them with tea and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiaoxian proposed recruiting merchants to transport grain to the frontier, repaying them in tea and salt.

sentences.zh: 召對稱旨，命馳驛陝西，與轉運使鄭文寶議立規畫，後多施行。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, his words matched the intent; he was ordered to ride post-haste to Shaanxi and with Transport Commissioner Zheng Wenbao discuss establishing regulations; many were later implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, he pleased the emperor and was dispatched post-haste to Shaanxi to work with Transport Commissioner Zheng Wenbao on a plan; much of it was later implemented.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Field Administration Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Vice Director of the Field Administration Bureau in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘗建置三司拘收司，以檢天下財利出入之數，詔如其請。

translations.literal: He once proposed establishing a Three Departments Collection and Recovery Office to inspect the figures of revenue and expenditure throughout the realm; an edict approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: He once proposed creating a Collection Office under the Three Departments to audit national revenue and expenditure; the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 知興元府，坐保任失實，降通判華州，徙知鄆州。

translations.literal: As prefect of Xingyuan Prefecture, he sat on guarantor recommendation being untrue and was demoted to deputy prefect of Huazhou, then transferred to prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Xingyuan, Sun Xiaoxian was demoted to deputy prefect of Huazhou for a false guarantor recommendation, then transferred to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宰相寇準舉，換內園使、知貝州。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Kou Zhun recommended him; he was exchanged to Internal Garden Commissioner and prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Kou Zhun recommended him; he was transferred to Internal Garden Commissioner and prefect of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 會慈州民張熙載詐稱黃河都總管，籍並河州郡芻糧數，至貝州。

translations.literal: It happened that a Cizhou commoner Zhang Xizai falsely claimed to be Chief Superintendent of the Yellow River, registered the forage counts of all Yellow River border prefectures and counties, and reached Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A Cizhou man named Zhang Xizai falsely claimed to be Chief Superintendent of the Yellow River, registered forage counts from all river-border prefectures, and made his way to Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 孝先覺其奸，捕繫獄。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian perceived his fraud and arrested and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiaoxian saw through the fraud, arrested Zhang, and jailed him.

sentences.zh: 孝先欲因此為奇功，以動朝廷，迫司理參軍紀瑛教熙載偽為契丹諜者，號景州刺史兼侍中、司空、大靈宮使，部送京師。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian wished thereby to make an extraordinary achievement to move the court; he compelled judicial assistant Ji Ying to teach Xizai to pose as a Khitan spy, styled Inspector of Jingzhou concurrent with Grand Counselor, Minister of Works, and Commissioner of the Great Spirit Palace, and escorted him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiaoxian hoped to turn the case into a spectacular triumph that would impress the court. He forced judicial assistant Ji Ying to coach Xizai into posing as a Khitan spy styled Inspector of Jingzhou, Grand Counselor, Minister of Works, and Commissioner of the Great Spirit Palace, then escorted him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 樞密院按得孝先所教狀，謫澤州都監，利、虢三州，改環慶路兵馬鈐轄、知邠州。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs investigated and obtained the coached deposition; he was demoted to inspector general of Zezhou and the prefectures of Li and Guo, then changed to military inspector of Huanqing Circuit and prefect of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs uncovered the coached testimony; Sun Xiaoxian was demoted to garrison commander of Zezhou covering Li and Guo prefectures, then reassigned as military inspector of Huanqing Circuit and prefect of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，領昭州刺史，為益州鈐轄，再遷左藏庫使，擢西上閤門使、涇原路鈐轄兼知渭州，復知邠州，徙耀州，以右領軍衛大將軍、昭州刺史，分司西京卒。

translations.literal: After a year he held the post of prefect of Zhaozhou, served as military inspector of Yizhou, was again promoted to Commissioner of the Left Repository, promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner, military inspector of Jingyuan Circuit concurrent with prefect of Weizhou, again prefect of Binzhou, transferred to Yaozhou, with Right General of the Right Lead Army Guard and prefect of Zhaozhou, and died while on nominal duty at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was prefect of Zhaozhou and military inspector of Yizhou. He was promoted to Commissioner of the Left Repository, then to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and military inspector of Jingyuan Circuit while serving as prefect of Weizhou. He served again at Binzhou, transferred to Yaozhou, and held the titles Right General of the Right Lead Army Guard and prefect of Zhaozhou when he died on nominal duty at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 子簡夫。

translations.literal: His son was Jianfu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jianfu.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 簡夫

translations.literal: Great-grandson: Jianfu
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson: Jianfu

sentences.zh: 簡夫，字太簡，隱居不仕。

translations.literal: Jianfu, style name Taijian, lived in seclusion and did not hold office.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfu, courtesy name Taijian, lived in retirement and refused office.

sentences.zh: 康定中，樞密使杜衍薦之，召見，以秘書省校書郎簽書秦州觀察判官。

translations.literal: In the Kangding era, Military Affairs Commissioner Du Yan recommended him; he was summoned for audience and, as proofreader of the Secretariat, signed as aide to the observation commissioner of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangding era, Military Affairs Commissioner Du Yan recommended him. Summoned to audience, he was appointed Secretariat proofreader and aide to the Qinzhou observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 公事既罷，居長安，自以處士起，不復肯隨眾調官，多為岐路求辟薦。

translations.literal: When public business ended, he resided in Chang'an; since he had risen as a retired scholar, he no longer wished to follow the crowd in seeking posts, but often took byways to seek recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: When his assignment ended he settled in Chang'an. Having entered service as a recluse, he refused the usual round of official transfers and instead cultivated side paths to fresh appointments.

sentences.zh: 時三白渠久廢，京兆府遂薦簡夫治渠事。

translations.literal: At the time the Three White Canals had long been abandoned; Jingzhao Prefecture then recommended Jianfu to manage canal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Three White Canals had long fallen into disuse; Jingzhao Prefecture then recommended Jianfu to restore them.

sentences.zh: 先時，治渠歲役六縣民四十日，用梢木數百萬，而水不足。

translations.literal: Previously, maintaining the canals annually conscripted the people of six counties for forty days, used millions of wooden stakes, yet water was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, canal maintenance drafted six counties for forty days each year, consumed millions of wooden stakes, and still yielded insufficient water.

sentences.zh: 簡夫用三十日，梢木比舊三之一，而水有餘。

translations.literal: Jianfu used thirty days; wooden stakes were one-third of the old amount, yet water was ample.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfu finished in thirty days, used one-third the timber, and produced a surplus of water.

sentences.zh: 知坊州，徙簡州，用張方平薦，知雅州。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Fangzhou, was transferred to Jianzhou, and on Zhang Fangping's recommendation became prefect of Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Fangzhou, transferred to Jianzhou, and on Zhang Fangping' recommendation was appointed prefect of Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 既而辰州蠻酋彭仕羲內寇，三司副使李參、侍御史朱處約安撫不能定，繼命簡夫往。

translations.literal: Before long the Chenzhou Miao chieftain Peng Shiyi raided within the borders; Three Departments Vice Commissioner Li Can and attendant censor Zhu Chuyue as pacification commissioners could not settle it; Jianfu was next ordered to go.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chenzhou Miao chieftain Peng Shiyi raided the interior. Vice Commissioner Li Can and Attendant Censor Zhu Chuyue failed to pacify the region; Jianfu was sent next.

sentences.zh: 至則督諸將進兵，築明溪上、下二砦，據其險要，拓取故省地石馬崖五百餘里。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he supervised the generals in advancing troops, built upper and lower Mingxi stockades, held their strategic points, and expanded to recover former provincial territory at Shima Cliff for more than five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he drove the generals forward, built upper and lower stockades at Mingxi to hold the strategic heights, and recovered more than five hundred li of former provincial territory at Shima Cliff.

sentences.zh: 仕羲內附。

translations.literal: Shiyi submitted from within.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 擢三司鹽鐵判官，以疾，知虢、同二州，累遷尚書職方員外郎，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to judge of the Three Departments Salt and Iron Monopoly; due to illness he served as prefect of Guo and Tong prefectures, was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War's Bureau of Assignments, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judge of the Salt and Iron Monopoly under the Three Departments. Illness later limited him to prefectures Guo and Tong; he rose to Vice Director of the Bureau of Assignments in the Ministry of War and died in office.

sentences.zh: 錄其子壽臣為郊社齋郎。

translations.literal: His son Shouchen was recorded as Sacrificial Officer of the Suburban and State Shrines.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouchen was granted the post of Sacrificial Officer at the Suburban and State Shrines.

sentences.zh: 簡夫始起隱者，出入乘牛，冠鐵冠，自號「山長」。

translations.literal: Jianfu at first rose from a hermit; going out and in he rode an ox, wore an iron cap, and styled himself "Mountain Elder."
translations.idiomatic: Jianfu had risen from the hermit life: he traveled by ox, wore an iron cap, and called himself the Mountain Elder.

sentences.zh: 關中用兵，以口舌捭闔公卿。

translations.literal: With warfare in Guanzhong, he used speech to maneuver among nobles and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: With war raging in Guanzhong, he talked his way among grandees and ministers.

sentences.zh: 既仕，自奉稍驕侈，騶御服飾，頓忘其舊，里閭指笑之曰：「牛及鐵冠安在？」

translations.literal: Once in office, his self-support became somewhat proud and extravagant; mounts, attendants, and adornments—he suddenly forgot his old ways; neighbors pointed and laughed, saying: "Where are the ox and iron cap?"
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he grew proud and extravagant—outriders, finery, his old self forgotten. Neighbors laughed and asked: "Where did the ox and iron cap go?"

sentences.zh: 王超，趙州人，弱冠長七尺餘。

translations.literal: Wang Chao was a man of Zhaozhou; at the capping age he stood more than seven chi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chao was from Zhaozhou; by his capping ceremony he stood over seven chi tall.

sentences.zh: 太宗尹京，召置麾下。

translations.literal: When Taizong governed the capital, he was summoned and placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong governed the capital as heir apparent, Wang Chao was summoned into his service.

sentences.zh: 及即位，以隸御龍直。

translations.literal: When he acceded, Chao was placed under the Imperial Dragon Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Chao was assigned to the Imperial Dragon Guard.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，累遷至河西軍節度使、殿前都虞候。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, he was repeatedly promoted to military commissioner of Hexi Army and Chief Commandant of the Palace Ward.
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Chunhua he had risen to military commissioner of the Hexi Army and Chief Commandant of the Palace Ward.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，以翊戴功，加檢校太傅、領天平軍節度。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded, for merit in supporting the enthronement he was additionally made Grand Preceptor with inspection and given concurrent command of Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded, Wang Chao was rewarded for supporting the enthronement with the honorary title Grand Preceptor and command of Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年秋，大閱禁兵二十萬於東郊，超執五方旗以節進退，上御戎幄觀之，面賜褒獎。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Xianping, two hundred thousand forbidden troops were grandly reviewed at the eastern suburb; Chao held the five-direction flags to regulate advance and retreat; the emperor viewed from the military pavilion and personally bestowed praise and reward.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the second year of Xianping, two hundred thousand palace troops were reviewed at the eastern suburb. Chao bore the five-direction flags to command the drill; the emperor watched from a military pavilion and praised him in person.

sentences.zh: 從幸大名，與都虞候張進並為先鋒。

translations.literal: Following the imperial visit to Daming, he and Chief Commandant Zhang Jin both served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Daming, Chao and Chief Commandant Zhang Jin served jointly as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 都大點檢傅潛逗撓得罪，以超為侍衛馬步軍都虞候、鎮州行營都部署，又帥鎮、定、高陽關三路。

translations.literal: Chief Inspector Fu Qian was punished for stalling; Chao was made Chief Commandant of the Palace Cavalry and Infantry and commander of the Zhenzhou field headquarters, and also commanded the three routes of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Inspector Fu Qian was punished for hesitation; Chao replaced him as Chief Commandant of the Palace Cavalry and Infantry and field commander at Zhenzhou, commanding the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass lines.

sentences.zh: 契丹入邊，與戰於遂城西，俘馘二萬計，斬其裨王騎將十五人，手詔褒美。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered the border, he fought west of Suicheng; captives and severed heads numbered about twenty thousand; fifteen of their secondary kings and cavalry commanders were beheaded; an imperial hand-edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan crossed the border he fought west of Suicheng, taking some twenty thousand heads and captives and killing fifteen Khitan princes and cavalry commanders. The emperor sent a personal edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷陷清遠軍，以超將西面行營之師禦之，徙帥永興軍。

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian seized Qingyuan Army, Chao was sent to command the western field army to resist him, and was transferred to command Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Jiqian seized Qingyuan Army, Chao was ordered to lead the western field army against him and was transferred to command Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 宰相言超材堪將帥，遂以超帥定州路行營，王繼忠副之。

translations.literal: Grand councilors said Chao's talent suited command; accordingly Chao was made commander of the Dingzhou Route field army, with Wang Jizhong as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councilors declared Chao fit for high command; he was made field commander on the Dingzhou Route with Wang Jizhong as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 尋加鎮、定、高陽關三路都部署，密遣中使賜以御弓矢，許便宜從事。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made overall commander of the three routes Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass; a palace envoy was secretly sent to bestow imperial bow and arrows, permitting discretionary action.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made overall commander of the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass lines. The emperor secretly sent a palace envoy with the imperial bow and arrows and authorization to act at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Grand General with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies and Grand Marshal with inspection.
translations.idiomatic: He received the honorary titles Grand General with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 咸平六年，遼師大入，超召鎮州桑贊、高陽關周瑩率兵會定州，瑩以非詔旨不至。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianping, Liao armies entered in force; Chao summoned Sang Zan of Zhenzhou and Zhou Ying of Gaoyang Pass to lead troops to rally at Dingzhou; Ying, saying it was not an imperial order, did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianping the Liao invaded in force. Chao summoned Sang Zan from Zhenzhou and Zhou Ying from Gaoyang Pass to rendezvous at Dingzhou; Ying refused, claiming no imperial order had reached him.

sentences.zh: 遼兵圍望都，超、贊率兵赴之，陣於縣南六里。

translations.literal: Liao troops besieged Wangdu; Chao and Zan led troops to the rescue and formed battle lines six li south of the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: Liao forces besieged Wangdu. Chao and Zan marched to relieve the city and drew up battle lines six li south of the county seat.

sentences.zh: 繼忠在陣東偏，契丹出其背，遮絕糧道，人馬乏困，繼忠馳前與契丹戰，超、贊遂旋師，繼忠孤軍沒焉。

translations.literal: Jizhong was on the eastern flank; the Khitan emerged behind them, cutting off the supply route; men and horses were exhausted; Jizhong galloped forward to fight the Khitan; Chao and Zan then wheeled the army about; Jizhong's isolated force was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong held the eastern flank. The Khitan struck from the rear and cut the supply line; men and horses were exhausted. Jizhong charged the Khitan alone while Chao and Zan withdrew—and Jizhong's isolated detachment was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 上即遣劉承珪、李允則馳往，察退衄之狀，且言鎮州副部署李福、拱聖軍都指揮使王昇當戰先旋，福坐削籍，流封州，昇決杖，配隸瓊州。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately sent Liu Chenggui and Li Yunze post-haste to investigate the circumstances of the retreat; it was also said that Zhenzhou deputy commander Li Fu and Chief Commander of the Palatial Sacred Army Wang Sheng turned back first in battle; Fu was struck from the rolls and exiled to Fengzhou; Sheng was sentenced to beating with the rod and assigned to Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately dispatched Liu Chenggui and Li Yunze to investigate the rout. Deputy commander Li Fu of Zhenzhou and Chief Commander Wang Sheng of the Palatial Sacred Army were found to have withdrawn first: Fu was struck from the rolls and exiled to Fengzhou; Sheng was flogged and assigned to Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，上親巡澶淵，召超赴行在，復緩師期，契丹遂深入。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, the emperor personally toured Chanyuan; Chao was summoned to the imperial camp but again delayed the army's schedule; the Khitan therefore penetrated deeply.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingde era the emperor went in person to Chanyuan and summoned Chao to the camp—but Chao again delayed, and the Khitan drove deep into Song territory.

sentences.zh: 會南北通好，故薄其責，止罷超三路帥，為崇信軍節度使，徙知河陽。

translations.literal: As north and south established friendly relations, his punishment was therefore lightened; only Chao's three-route command was removed; he was made military commissioner of Chongxin Army and transferred to prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Peace was restored between north and south, so his punishment was light: he was merely stripped of the three-route command, appointed military commissioner of Chongxin Army, and transferred to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 又移鎮建雄，知青州，卒。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to command Jianxiong, served as prefect of Qingzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to command Jianxiong and serve as prefect of Qingzhou, and died there.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，再贈尚書令，追封魯國公，諡武康。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, again posthumously granted Director of the Department of State Affairs, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, and given the posthumous title Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, then as Director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, and given the posthumous name Wukang ("Martial and Steadfast").

sentences.zh: 超為將善部分，御下有恩。

translations.literal: As a general Chao was good at deploying forces and showed kindness to subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Chao was skilled at disposition and generous to his men.

sentences.zh: 與高瓊同典禁旅，嘗休假他適，過營壘，軍校不時將迎，瓊即命箠罰，超以為非公行，不當加罪，人稱其恕。

translations.literal: He and Gao Qiong jointly commanded the forbidden guard; once on leave going elsewhere he passed a camp; a military officer did not timely go out to receive him; Qiong immediately ordered beating punishment; Chao thought it was not an official journey and should not incur punishment; people praised his forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: He and Gao Qiong jointly commanded the palace guard. Once on personal leave Chao passed a camp whose officer failed to salute in time; Qiong ordered him beaten, but Chao argued that an unofficial journey should not be punished—people praised his forbearance.

sentences.zh: 然臨軍寡謀，拙於戰鬥。

translations.literal: Yet facing armies he lacked strategy and was clumsy in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the field he lacked stratagem and proved awkward in combat.

sentences.zh: 子德用。

translations.literal: His son was Dezuo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Wang Dezuo.

sentences.zh: 子 德用

translations.literal: Son: Dezuo
translations.idiomatic: Son: Wang Dezuo

sentences.zh: 德用，字元輔。

translations.literal: Dezuo, style name Yuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dezuo, courtesy name Yuanfu.

sentences.zh: 父超為懷州防禦使，補衙內都指揮使。

translations.literal: When his father Chao was defense commissioner of Huaizhou, he was appointed acting commander of the yamen guard.
translations.idiomatic: While his father Chao served as defense commissioner of Huaizhou, Dezuo was appointed commander of the yamen guard.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，分五路出兵擊李繼遷，超帥兵六萬出綏、夏，德用年十七，為先鋒，將萬人戰鐵門關，斬首十三級，俘掠畜產以數萬計。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, five routes sent troops to strike Li Jiqian; Chao commanded sixty thousand troops out through Sui and Xia; Dezuo at age seventeen served as vanguard, leading ten thousand men to fight at Tiemen Pass, beheading thirteen, and capturing and plundering livestock numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao five armies marched against Li Jiqian; Chao led sixty thousand men through Sui and Xia. Dezuo, seventeen, served as vanguard with ten thousand men, fought at Tiemen Pass, took thirteen heads, and captured tens of thousands of livestock.

sentences.zh: 進師烏白池，他將多失道不至，虜銳甚，超按兵不進，德用請乘之，得精兵五千，轉戰三日，敵勢卻。

translations.literal: Advancing to Wubai Pool, other generals mostly lost the way and did not arrive; the enemy was very sharp; Chao held the army without advancing; Dezuo requested to strike while their momentum held; he obtained five thousand picked troops, fought in turning battles for three days, and the enemy's momentum receded.
translations.idiomatic: At Wubai Pool most allied generals lost their way and never arrived. The enemy was fierce; Chao held back. Dezuo asked leave to strike, took five thousand elite troops, and fought for three days until the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 德用曰：「歸師迫險必亂。」

translations.literal: Dezuo said: "An army returning pressed by peril will surely fall into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Dezuo said, "A retreat through dangerous ground is sure to turn into a rout."

sentences.zh: 乃領兵距夏州五十里，絕其歸路，下令曰：「亂行者斬！」

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops fifty li from Xiazhou, cutting off their retreat, and ordered: "Whoever moves in disorder will be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: He then took up a position fifty li from Xiazhou and blocked the retreat, ordering: "Break ranks and die!"

sentences.zh: 一軍肅然，超亦為之按轡。

translations.literal: The whole army was solemn; Chao also therefore checked his reins.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army held its order; even Chao tightened his grip on the reins.

sentences.zh: 繼遷躡其後，左右望見隊伍甚嚴整，莫敢近。

translations.literal: Jiqian followed behind; those left and right looked and saw the ranks very strict and orderly, and none dared approach.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiqian pursued from the rear, but his scouts saw ranks so disciplined that none dared close.

sentences.zh: 超撫其背曰：「王氏有子矣。」

translations.literal: Chao patted his back and said: "The Wang family has a son!"
translations.idiomatic: Chao clapped him on the back and said, "The Wang family has borne a son!"

sentences.zh: 累遷內殿崇班，以御前忠佐為馬軍都軍頭，出為邢、洺、磁、相巡檢。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Honored Company of the Inner Hall; as a Trusted Assistant Before the Throne he served as Chief Commander of the Horse Army; he went out as inspector of Xing, Ming, Ci, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Honored Company of the Inner Hall and Chief Commander of the Horse Army as a Trusted Assistant Before the Throne, then served as military inspector of Xing, Ming, Ci, and Xiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 盜張洪霸相聚界上，吏不能捕。

translations.literal: The bandit Zhang Hongba gathered men on the border; officials could not capture him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Zhang Hongba gathered a gang on the border that officials could not break.

sentences.zh: 德用以氈車載勇士，詐為婦人飾，過邯鄲。

translations.literal: Dezuo used felt-covered carts carrying brave warriors, disguised as women's adornment, and passed through Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Dezuo loaded brave men into felt-covered carts disguised as a women's procession and passed through Handan.

sentences.zh: 賊果來邀，勇士奮出，悉禽之。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed came to intercept; the warriors burst out and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits took the bait; the warriors sprang out and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 徙督捕陝西東路，盜賊相戒曰：「此禽張洪霸者。」

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervise capture on the Eastern Route of Shaanxi; bandits warned one another, saying: "This is the one who captured Zhang Hongba."
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to supervise capture on Shaanxi's Eastern Route, bandits warned one another: "This is the man who took Zhang Hongba."

sentences.zh: 皆相率逃去。

translations.literal: They all fled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: They fled in droves.

sentences.zh: 為環慶路指揮使，尋以奏事忤旨，責授鄆州馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: He served as commander of Huanqing Circuit; soon for memorializing affairs contrary to the intent he was punished with appointment as Chief Commander of Cavalry and Infantry of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commander of Huanqing Circuit but was demoted to Chief Commander of Yanzhou's cavalry and infantry after a memorial displeased the throne.

sentences.zh: 歷內殿直都虞候、殿前左班都虞候、柳州刺史，遷捧日左廂都指揮使、英州團練使。

translations.literal: He served as Chief Commandant of the Inner Hall Guard, Chief Commandant of the Left Division Before the Palace, and prefect of Liuzhou; he was promoted to Chief Commander of the Left Wing of the Sun-Rising Guard and regimental commissioner of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Chief Commandant of the Inner Hall Guard, Chief Commandant of the Left Division Before the Palace, and prefect of Liuzhou, then became Chief Commander of the Left Wing of the Sun-Rising Guard and regimental commissioner of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，以博州團練使知廣信軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng, as regimental commissioner of Bozhou he served as prefect of Guangxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tiansheng era he served as military prefect of Guangxin Army with the rank of regimental commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 城壞久不治，德用率禁軍增築之，有詔褒諭。

translations.literal: The walls were ruined and long unrepaired; Dezuo led forbidden troops to enlarge and build them; an edict praised and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The walls had long lain in ruins; Dezuo led palace troops to rebuild and extend them, earning an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 徙冀州，歷龍神衛、捧日天武四廂都指揮使、康州防禦使、侍衛親軍步軍馬軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jizhou, served as Chief Commander of the four wings of Dragon Spirit Guard, Sun-Rising and Heavenly Martial guards, defense commissioner of Kangzhou, and Chief Commandant of the Palace Guard's infantry and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to Jizhou and rose through Chief Commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit, Sun-Rising, and Heavenly Martial guards, defense commissioner of Kangzhou, and Chief Commandant of the palace guard infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 召還，又為幷代州馬步軍副都總管，遷殿前都虞候、步軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: Summoned back, he again served as deputy overall commander of Bing and Dai prefectures' cavalry and infantry; he was promoted to Chief Commandant Before the Palace and Deputy Chief Commander of the infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he served as deputy overall commander of Bing and Dai's cavalry and infantry, then as Chief Commandant Before the Palace and Deputy Chief Commander of the infantry.

sentences.zh: 歷桂州、福州觀察使。

translations.literal: He served as observation commissioner of Guizhou and Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as observation commissioner of Guizhou and Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后臨朝，有求內降補軍吏者，德用曰：「補吏，軍政也，不可與。」

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian held court, someone sought an internal edict to appoint a military clerk; Dezuo said: "Appointing clerks is military administration—it cannot be granted."
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian held court, someone sought an informal edict to install a military clerk. Dezuo replied, "Clerk appointments are military affairs. They cannot be granted by private favor."

sentences.zh: 太后固欲與之，卒不奉詔，乃止。

translations.literal: The empress dowager firmly wished to grant it; he ultimately did not obey the edict, and it then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager insisted, but he refused the edict to the end, and the matter dropped.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，有司請衛士坐甲，德用曰：「非故事也。」

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, responsible officials requested the guards sit in armor; Dezuo said: "That is not precedent."
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager's death officials asked that the guard stand under arms. Dezuo said, "That is not precedent."

sentences.zh: 不奉詔。

translations.literal: He did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the order.

sentences.zh: 仁宗閱太后閣中，得德用前奏軍吏事，奇之，以為可大用，拜檢校太保、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong reviewed the empress dowager's pavilion and obtained Dezuo's earlier memorial on the military clerk matter; he marveled at it, thought him fit for great employment, and appointed him Grand Lord of Suppression with inspection and Concurrent Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong, reviewing the late empress dowager's papers, found Dezuo's memorial on the clerk appointment and was impressed. Deeming him fit for high office, he appointed him Grand Lord of Suppression and Concurrent Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 德用謝曰：「臣武人，幸得以馳驅自效，賴陛下威靈，待罪行間足矣。

translations.literal: Dezuo declined, saying: "Your subject is a military man; fortunate to be able to serve by galloping in battle, relying on Your Majesty's august power; holding office by grace of punishment is already enough.
translations.idiomatic: Dezuo demurred: "I am a soldier, Your Majesty, fortunate to serve at the saddle. To hold office by your grace is honor enough.

sentences.zh: 且臣不學，不足以當大事。」

translations.literal: Moreover your subject has no learning and is insufficient to undertake great affairs."
translations.idiomatic: I am unlettered and unfit for great affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者趣入院，遂為副使。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to urge him to enter the bureau; he then became vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to hurry him into office, and he became vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 久之，以奉國軍節度觀察留後同知院事，遷知院。

translations.literal: After a long time, as military commissioner observer and acting prefect of Fengguo Army he jointly managed bureau affairs, and was promoted to bureau commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In time, as acting military commissioner of Fengguo Army he served jointly at the bureau and was promoted to commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歷安德軍，加檢校太尉、定國軍節度使、宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: He commanded Ande Army, was additionally made Grand Marshal with inspection, military commissioner of Dingguo Army, and commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Ande Army and received the titles Grand Marshal, military commissioner of Dingguo Army, and commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 趙元昊反，德用請自將討之，不許。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, Dezuo requested to personally lead troops to suppress him; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, Dezuo asked to lead the campaign himself; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 德用狀貌雄毅，面黑，頸以下白晰，人皆異之。

translations.literal: Dezuo's appearance was heroic and resolute; his face was black; from the neck down he was fair—everyone considered him strange.
translations.idiomatic: Dezuo was rugged in bearing, with a dark face and fair skin from the neck down—a combination people found striking.

sentences.zh: 言者論德用貌類藝祖，御史中丞孔道輔繼言之，且謂德用得士心，不宜久典機密，遂罷為武寧軍節度使、徐州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Critics argued Dezuo's appearance resembled Taizu; Censor-in-Chief Kong Daofu repeated this, and moreover said Dezuo had won soldiers' hearts and should not long hold confidential matters; he was therefore dismissed to military commissioner of Wuning Army and chief secretary of Xuzhou Superior Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Critics claimed Dezuo resembled Emperor Taizu in appearance; Censor-in-Chief Kong Daofu said the same and added that he had won the army's loyalty and should not long hold confidential power. He was dismissed to military commissioner of Wuning Army and chief secretary of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 有言德用市馬於府州者，上其券，乃市於商人者。

translations.literal: Someone said Dezuo bought horses at Fuzhou; the vouchers were submitted, and they turned out to be bought from merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Accusers claimed Dezuo had traded for horses at Fuzhou; the receipts showed ordinary purchases from merchants.

sentences.zh: 言者猶不已，降右千牛衛上將軍、知隨州，州置判官，家人皆惶恐，德用舉止言色如平時，惟不接賓客而已。

translations.literal: The accusers still did not stop; he was demoted to Senior General of the Right Wing of the Thousand-Ox Guard and prefect of Suizhou; the prefecture was given an administrative aide; his family all were fearful; Dezuo's bearing, speech, and expression were as in normal times, only not receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: The accusations continued; he was demoted to Senior General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and prefect of Suizhou—with an overseer appointed to the prefecture. His household panicked, but Dezuo's manner never changed; he merely stopped receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 徙知曹州，或謂德用曰：「孔中丞害公，今死矣。」

translations.literal: Transferred to serve as prefect of Caozhou, someone said to Dezuo: "Censor Kong harmed you; he is dead now."
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Caozhou, someone told Dezuo, "Censor Kong ruined you—and he is dead now."

sentences.zh: 德用曰：「中丞言官，豈害我者？

translations.literal: Dezuo said: "The censor was a remonstrating official—how could he have been one who harmed me?
translations.idiomatic: Dezuo replied, "The censor spoke as an official remonstrator. How could he have harmed me?

sentences.zh: 朝廷亡一忠臣，可惜也。」

translations.literal: The court has lost a loyal minister—it is regrettable."
translations.idiomatic: The court has lost a loyal minister. That is the real pity."

sentences.zh: 起為保靜軍節度觀察留後、知青州，改澶州。

translations.literal: He was restored as acting military governor and observer of Baojing Army and prefect of Qing Prefecture, then transferred to Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as acting military governor and observer of Baojing Army and prefect of Qing Prefecture, then transferred to Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陝西用兵久無功，契丹遣劉六符來求復關南地，以兵壓境。

translations.literal: The western campaign had long gone without success; the Khitan sent Liu Liufu to demand return of the Guannan lands, pressing the border with troops.
translations.idiomatic: The western campaign had long failed; the Khitan sent Liu Liufu to demand return of the Guannan lands, pressing the border with troops.

sentences.zh: 德用見帝，流涕言：「臣前被罪，陛下赦而不誅，今不足辱命。」

translations.literal: Dezuo saw the emperor and, weeping, said: "Your subject was once punished; Your Majesty pardoned and did not execute me—now I am unworthy of this commission."
translations.idiomatic: Dezuo saw the emperor and wept: "Your subject was once punished; Your Majesty spared my life—I am unworthy of this commission."

sentences.zh: 帝慰勞，曰：「河北方警，借卿鎮撫之。」

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him and said: "Hebei is now alarmed—I borrow you to pacify it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him: "Hebei is alarmed—I borrow you to pacify it."

sentences.zh: 又賜手詔慰勉，拜保靜軍節度使。

translations.literal: He also granted a hand-edict of consolation and encouragement and made him military governor of Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted a hand-edict of encouragement and made him military governor of Baojing Army.

sentences.zh: 歲大熟，六符見德用拜曰：「此公仁政所及也。」

translations.literal: That year the harvest was abundant; Liufu saw Dezuo and bowed, saying: "This is the reach of the lord's benevolent rule."
translations.idiomatic: That year the harvest was abundant; Liufu saw Dezuo and bowed, saying, "This is the reach of your benevolent rule."

sentences.zh: 徙真定府、定州路都總管，還奏事，復以宣徽南院使判成德軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to overall commander of Zhending Prefecture and the Ding Prefecture Route; returning to report, he was again made Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Domestic Service and regent of Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to overall commander of Zhending and the Ding Prefecture Route; returning to report, he was again made Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Domestic Service and regent of Chengde Army.

sentences.zh: 未行，徙定州路都總管。

translations.literal: Before he departed he was transferred to overall commander of the Ding Prefecture Route.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed he was transferred to overall commander of the Ding Prefecture Route.

sentences.zh: 日訓練士卒，久之，士殊可用。

translations.literal: Daily he trained soldiers; after long time the troops were exceptionally usable.
translations.idiomatic: He trained soldiers daily; in time the troops became exceptionally capable.

sentences.zh: 契丹使諜者來覘，或請捕殺之，德用曰：「第舍之，彼得實以告，是服人之兵以不戰也。」

translations.literal: The Khitan sent spies to reconnoiter; some asked to capture and kill them. Dezuo said: "Just let them go—they will report the truth, which is to subdue the enemy's troops without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent spies; some asked to capture and kill them. Dezuo said, "Just let them go—they will report the truth, subduing the enemy without fighting."

sentences.zh: 明日大閱，援桴鼓之士皆踴躍，進退坐作，終日不戮一人。

translations.literal: The next day he held a grand review; the drum-beating troops all leaped with spirit, advancing, retreating, sitting, and forming ranks; all day not one man was punished.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he held a grand review; drum-beating troops leaped with spirit in advance, retreat, sitting, and forming ranks; all day not one man was punished.

sentences.zh: 乃下令：「具糗糧，聽吾鼓聲，視吾旗幟所向。」

translations.literal: He then ordered: "Prepare dry rations, listen for my drum, and follow my banners."
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered, "Prepare dry rations, listen for my drum, and follow my banners."

sentences.zh: 覘者歸告契丹，謂漢兵將大入。

translations.literal: The spies returned and told the Khitan that Han troops were about to invade in force.
translations.idiomatic: The spies returned and told the Khitan Han troops were about to invade in force.

sentences.zh: 既而復議和，遂徙陳州，又徙河陽。

translations.literal: Shortly peace was discussed again and he was transferred to Chen Prefecture, then Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly peace was discussed again and he was transferred to Chen Prefecture, then Heyang.

sentences.zh: 不行，入奉朝請，出判相州，拜同中書門下平章事、判澶州。

translations.literal: He did not go, entered court attendance, went out as regent of Xiang Prefecture, and was made Grand Councilor and regent of Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He did not go, entered court attendance, went out as regent of Xiang Prefecture, and was made Grand Councilor and regent of Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徙鄭州，封祁國公，還，為會靈觀使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zheng Prefecture, enfeoffed Duke of Qi, returned, and was made Commissioner of the Huiling Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Zheng Prefecture, enfeoffed Duke of Qi, returned, and was made Commissioner of the Huiling Shrine.

sentences.zh: 德用素善射，雖老不衰。

translations.literal: Dezuo had long been skilled at archery and, though old, did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Dezuo had long excelled at archery and, though old, did not decline.

sentences.zh: 侍射瑞聖園，辭曰：「臣老矣，不能勝弓矢。」

translations.literal: Attending an archery party at Ruicheng Garden, he declined, saying: "Your subject is old and can no longer manage bow and arrow."
translations.idiomatic: Attending archery at Ruicheng Garden, he declined: "Your subject is old and can no longer manage bow and arrow."

sentences.zh: 帝再三諭之，持二矢未發。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly urged him; he held two arrows without loosing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly urged him; he held two arrows without loosing.

sentences.zh: 帝顧之，使必中，乃收弓矢謝，一發中的，再發又中。

translations.literal: The emperor looked at him and ordered him to hit the target; he then put away bow and arrows and thanked him; one shot hit the mark, a second shot hit again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked at him and ordered him to hit; he put away bow and arrows and thanked him; one shot hit, a second hit again.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「德用欲中即中爾，孰謂老且衰乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said: "When Dezuo wishes to hit, he hits—who says he is old and failing?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled: "When Dezuo wishes to hit, he hits—who says he is old and failing?"

sentences.zh: 賜襲衣、金帶，加檢校太師，復判鄭州，徙澶州，改集慶軍節度使，封冀國公。

translations.literal: He was granted a robe of honor, gold belt, additionally made Grand Preceptor, again regent of Zheng Prefecture, transferred to Cao Prefecture, changed to military governor of Jiqing Army, and enfeoffed Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a robe of honor and gold belt, additionally made Grand Preceptor, again regent of Zheng Prefecture, transferred to Cao Prefecture, changed to military governor of Jiqing Army, and enfeoffed Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 皇祐三年，上疏乞骸骨，以太子太師致仕，大朝會綴中書門下班。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangyou he submitted a memorial begging to retire; he retired as Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince and at grand court assemblies stood at the end of the Grand Councilor rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangyou he memorialized begging to retire; he retired as Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince and at grand court assemblies stood at the end of the Grand Councilor rank.

sentences.zh: 德用將家子，習知軍中情偽，善以恩撫下，故多得士心。

translations.literal: Dezuo was born to a military family, thoroughly knew the truth and falsehood of army affairs, and was good at winning subordinates with kindness; therefore he mostly won soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Born to a military family, Dezuo thoroughly knew army affairs and won subordinates with kindness; therefore he mostly won soldiers' hearts.

sentences.zh: 雖屢臨邊境，未嘗親矢石、督攻戰，而名聞四夷，閭閻婦女小兒，皆呼德用曰「黑王相公」。

translations.literal: Though he repeatedly faced the frontier, he never personally braved arrows and stones or directed assaults in battle, yet his name was heard in the four quarters; women and children in lanes and alleys all called Dezuo "Black Wang the Grand Councilor."
translations.idiomatic: Though he repeatedly faced the frontier and never personally braved arrows or directed assaults, his name was heard in the four quarters; lane women and alley children all called him "Black Wang the Grand Councilor."

sentences.zh: 帝嘗遣使問邊事，德用曰：「咸平、景德中，賜諸將陣圖，人皆死守戰法，緩急不相救，以至於屢敗。

translations.literal: The emperor once sent an envoy to ask about frontier affairs; Dezuo said: "In the Xianping and Jingde eras battle arrays were bestowed on the generals; each man clung to the prescribed formation, would not rescue one another in urgency, and thus was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sent an envoy to ask about frontier affairs; Dezuo said, "In Xianping and Jingde battle arrays were bestowed on generals; each clung to prescribed formations, would not rescue one another in urgency, and was repeatedly defeated.

sentences.zh: 誠願不以陣圖賜諸將，使得應變出奇，自立異效。」

translations.literal: I truly wish battle arrays not be bestowed on generals, so they may respond to change with surprise and establish distinctive achievements of their own."
translations.idiomatic: I truly wish battle arrays not be bestowed on generals, so they may respond to change with surprise and establish achievements of their own."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 德用諸子中，咸融最鍾愛，晚年頗縱之，多不法，後更折節自飭，官至左藏庫使、眉州防禦使。

translations.literal: Among Dezuo's sons Xianrong was most beloved; in his later years he indulged him rather freely and Xianrong often acted unlawfully; later he again restrained himself and was made Commissioner of the Left Repository and defense commissioner of Mei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Among Dezuo's sons Xianrong was most beloved; in later years he indulged him freely and Xianrong often acted unlawfully; later Xianrong restrained himself and was made Commissioner of the Left Repository and defense commissioner of Mei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 論曰：全義、德驤，遇知太祖、太宗，超復翊戴真宗，宜致崇顯，然堇堇無踰人者，而各有子勒勳於國籍。

translations.literal: Discussion: Quanyi and Dexiang met with recognition from Taizu and Taizong; Chao again supported Zhenzong's enthronement—they deserved high eminence, yet each barely surpassed others, and each had a son who carved merit into the national records.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion: Quanyi and Dexiang won recognition from Taizu and Taizong; Chao again supported Zhenzong's enthronement—they deserved eminence, yet each barely surpassed others, and each had a son who carved merit into the national records.

sentences.zh: 若知節生將家，喜讀書，立朝爭事，以剛正稱天下，其邦之司直歟！

translations.literal: As for Zhijie, born to a military family yet fond of books, contending in court affairs and famed throughout the realm for stern uprightness—is he not the upright officer of the state!
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie, born to a military family yet fond of books, contending in court and famed for stern uprightness—is he not the state's upright officer!

sentences.zh: 有終起進士，明幹知兵，平蜀鉅賊，振聲鄰敵，可謂「肇敏戎公」矣。

translations.literal: Youzhong rose from the jinshi, was bright and capable and knew war, pacified the great Shu rebel, and shook neighboring enemies—he may be called one who "first showed keenness in military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong rose from the jinshi, was bright and capable and knew war, pacified the great Shu rebel, and shook neighboring enemies—he may be called one who "first showed keenness in military affairs."

sentences.zh: 至於精神折衝，名聞四夷，矯矯虎臣，則德用其有焉。

translations.literal: As for spirit that overawed the foe, name heard in the four quarters—a fierce tiger among ministers—Dezuo had that in him.
translations.idiomatic: As for spirit that overawed the foe and name heard in the four quarters—a fierce tiger among ministers—Dezuo had that in him.
